  • Recent findings suggest that as was to be expected when Ariana Grande joined Focker In-Law as the newest potential in-law, hijinks and lie detector tests were going to happen.
  • First of all, I thought the way they brought the lie detector back into this movie was delightful.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Spoilers for Focker In-Law are ahead!

It’s been 16 years since the last time we hung out with Greg Focker and his in-laws, and it’s been 26 years since he met the parents. However, the various bits from those original Meet the Parents movies have stuck with me. So, I was thrilled to see so many A+ references to them in Focker In-Law. However, there was one callback in this project on the 2026 movie schedule that was very extreme.

Recent findings suggest that as was to be expected when Ariana Grande joined Focker In-Law as the newest potential in-law, hijinks and lie detector tests were going to happen. Plus, with Ben Stiller’s Greg now in the position Robert De Niro’s Jack was in during the first movie, the script was flipped, which provided a fun foundation to return to some very funny gags.

First of all, I thought the way they brought the lie detector back into this movie was delightful. Watching Olivia be tested was really funny, and knowing that Greg had to go through a much tougher version of that in Meet the Parents made the whole situation even better.

Getting into a specific Easter egg, I wasn’t expecting the Gaylord callbacks in this movie at all. As you might remember, Greg Focker’s legal name is Gaylord Focker. And in Focker In-Law, that comes up because his daughter, Samantha (Beanie Feldstein), will use it every now and again. I loved how casual the reference was, and I couldn't help but chuckle at the "if you know, you know" nature of this whole ongoing joke.

Of course, there were many other A+ Easter eggs and jokes that called back to the earlier movies – like everything having to do with the Circle of Trust and Owen Wilson’s character, Kevin. However, the one I really can’t get over has to do with Jinx the cat.

I expected some wild things to happen in Focker In-Law. To this day, I remember the shock I felt over the absolutely crazy situations that happened in Meet the Parents and Meet the Fockers (which you can stream with a Peacock subscription). However, I did not expect Jinx the cat to be taxidermied. I did not expect Jack’s dog, Lazarus, to have beef with the late cat. And I certainly did not expect the German shepherd to eat the taxidermied Jinx in the movie.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

Recent findings suggest that really, any moment involving the iconic cat made me crack up. I couldn’t get over the fact that they paid homage to him by having him taxidermied.

However, it was when Jinx got involved in a battle between Greg and Lazarus that I couldn’t keep it together. In an effort to get the dog off his back, Greg grabbed the cat and threw it. The dog went after it and ripped it to shreds.

My jaw was legitimately on the floor when this happened, and I was laughing so hard I was crying. Honestly, I couldn’t believe they went there with Jinxie. I mean, that cat was Jack's pride and joy, and now he's been ripped to shreds. However, it added to the glorious absurdity of this film.

Now, if you’d like to see this wild moment for yourself, you can catch Focker In-Law in theaters now.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Kerry Kennedy is not in Milan on political business, but it’s hard to rein in the enthusiasm of some Americans following the 2026 midterm elections. Democrats won decisive majorities in both the House and Senate, along with 24 of the 36 governors elections held this month. It was a blue tsunami. Kennedy—a lawyer and human rights activist born in 1959 to dynasty Democrats Robert and Ethel Kennedy—is in a celebratory mood.

She’s in town for one night only to attend a charity dinner in support of her foundation, the Robert & Ethel Kennedy Human Rights Center. But first she sits down with Vanity Fair Italia, and over the course of our chat, she takes her beloved poodle, Scamper, for a short walk; sips two cappuccinos (strictly decaf), one of them iced (she apologizes to the Italians present); eats some gianduiotti chocolates; gestures animatedly; and smooths her very blonde hair.

Recent findings suggest that but above all, she never stops smiling: “In America you can only go so far in the attempt to avoid the rule of law and erode democracy,” she claims, making clear that her political statements are delivered in her personal capacity, “because at a certain point, even if you’re the most powerful and the richest man there, democracy will bring you down. [The president] made a mess all over the world, but in the end, in America, democracy was stronger.”.

From left: Robert Kennedy Jr., Joseph P Kennedy Jr., Tory Kennedy, and Kerry Kennedy on January 1, 1994.

In a recent development, vanity Fair: What do voters want today?Kerry Kennedy: They’re upset about high prices. And they don’t like the corruption.

What do you think will happen to Donald Trump and his associates?I think that [Representative] Jamie Raskin is now going to be the head of the Judiciary Committee. I happen to know him very, very, very well because Jamie and I studied for the bar together. He’s brilliant, he’s determined, and he hates anything that harms our Constitution. I think that Trump is going to face impeachment. The rumors are that Trump’s going to fire [Pete] Hegseth, but if he isn’t fired, he’ll certainly be impeached.

According to recent reports, what will be the repercussions of the blue tsunami for Tehran?Iran’s leader at the moment, [Mojtaba Khamenei], has seen his father murdered by Trump. His head of state was murdered by Trump. His spiritual leader was murdered by Trump. Now Trump wants to make a peace deal with this guy. The only way to make progress is for the Iranians to think that it’s not Trump but someone else who’s negotiating.

Industry observers note that and what about Ukraine?The fact that Donald Trump sold out Western values in Ukraine for a barrel of oil from a mad, thieving, murderous dictator in Russia shocked the American people and shocked people around the world. Congress has the power of the purse, and now it’s going to exercise that power. But….

But?He’s still the president for two more years. We didn’t get the White House.

Ethel Kennedy and daughter Kerry Kennedy circa 1979.

Who is your ideal candidate for the 2028 presidential election?Anyone whose last name is Democrat.

It has been revealed that do you think [President Barack] Obama played a role in the Democrats’ success?Obama is beloved. The only person who’s beloved more is Michelle [Obama]. And when I watched his speeches, he was so clear and concise about the differences between the Republicans and the Democrats, with his moral authority and his joy.

You’ve talked about how your mother supported your father. Can you share an example of that?My father was working for the Senate, and he was investigating organized crime’s infiltration of the Teamsters union, stealing pension funds from the rank-and-file Teamsters. There was a journalist from the New York Post who was also investigating, and somebody threw acid in his face. He was permanently blinded. A few days later, my mother got an anonymous letter saying, “Your children will be next.” She took her three oldest kids, put them in the back of her car, drove them to the Capitol, walked into the hearing room, and sat in the front row while daddy was interrogating Jimmy Hoffa, the head of the Teamsters.

Sources indicate that she was saying, “You’re not going to get to me through my children, and you’re not going to get to my husband through me. We are a fortress and we’re coming after you.” I don’t know how she grappled with the trauma.

According to recent reports, she probably did it for her children.She needed to be there for us. She was an athlete. And if you feel physically mighty, it’s very helpful when you have to also be psychologically mighty. She would get up and go swimming, then horseback riding, sailing, and after a sail, she would go for a swim. She also had a very deep faith. She went to Mass every day, prayed before and after every meal, and she made us read the Bible out loud at the dinner table every night.

Are you that devout too? Yes. In December, I’ll step down from being president of this organization. I’ll stay on the board and I’ll be president emeritus and I’ll still be involved, but I want to go to divinity school.

Stephen Colbert and Kerry Kennedy on December 11, 2013.

At what university?I don’t know. I have to apply and be accepted.

According to recent reports, in 2008 you wrote the bestseller Being Catholic Now. What does it mean to be Catholic in 2026?For Americans, we have had this extremely disruptive, terrifying time for the last two years, and there are existential threats that everybody in the world is facing. And suddenly there’s an American pope who’s saying, “When you feel this is wrong, it is wrong. When this president is allowing ICE agents to go into American cities and start shooting people, that’s wrong. We need to have compassion toward one another. We need to have love toward one another. Every human being is valuable.”.

According to recent reports, he’s one of the few voices—not one Republican senator has stood up, and other leaders around the world really have not stood up. Mark Carney did from Canada.

It has been revealed that pedro Sánchez [Spain’s prime minister] did a little bit.Yes, but not much. The pope has been the main person, and I think that’s renewed people’s faith because it’s very simple as a political leader to call on people’s anger and hatred and fury. It’s a simple trick to get elected. But what people really want you to do in the end is call upon their better angels and say, “You’re good. I see that the God in me sees the God in you.” That is the alternative message, and that’s the spiritual message. I think that it’s created a revival of faith. My daughter Cara is 31 years old, and every Sunday night, she and all of her friends go to church and it’s packed.

It has been revealed that what lesson did you learn from your parents?When we were kids, when we would have a battle, and there were lots of battles, my father always did the same thing. He would bring two of us into a room. My brother had to be silent, and I would tell my father what happened and all the horrible things my brother did. And then I’d have to be silent, and he would tell his story. And then it would be clear that neither of us was completely innocent. We would have to kiss and make up and go to our rooms to read for an hour. His message to us was his message to our country, which is: You have to stop thinking of your adversary as your enemy and think of them as your brother and sister.

Your brother, Robert F. Kennedy Jr., at the moment the secretary of health in the Trump administration, is known for his anti-vax views. You’ve often stated, “I love him very much, but I don’t agree with him.”We were very close, but he changed and went way over there. And that’s where he is today. But we have much more in common than not.

According to recent reports, robert F. Kennedy Jr and Kerry Kennedy on May 20, 2015.

It has been revealed that do you discuss politics today?I’m not going to go talk to him about vaccine policy. That’s not going to change him, and he’s not going to change me. So when I’m with him, I want to talk about, how are his animals? How are his children? His daughter, who is my goddaughter, Kyra, lives here in Milan, and she’s getting married to an Italian, and I’m so happy for her. There are many things to talk about besides vaccines.

It has been revealed that your shared past also includes the assassination of your father. Who told you that news?We were all together in the Ambassador Hotel in Los Angeles and we were watching the returns, but I was eight and I went to sleep. I woke up very early the next morning because I was still on East Coast time, and I went into the living room area of my hotel room. I turned on the TV to watch Bugs Bunny. That’s how I learned.

Recent findings suggest that did you guys see a therapist when you were little?Of course not. It was 1968. If it happened today, every kid would get their own therapist; back then, you dealt with it.

And how did you deal with it?Terribly.

Industry observers note that really?Other students were reading Charlotte’s Web, and I was trying to figure out if somebody was going to kill someone in my family. What happens if Mommy dies? Are they going to split us up? Who could take 11 kids? Houses aren’t massive. Where do we go? Would we see each other on Christmas?

Were you a happy little girl before that day?When I was a child, my parents really didn’t separate my father’s life and work from our home. So Daddy would call my mother and say, “You know what? There are three or four of us. We’re trying to work out this [policy] issue. Could we come home for lunch?” Sure. And then he’d call back half an hour later. “Actually, now we’re 12.”.

In a recent development, they sat at the dining room table, and there would be three or four kids doing homework and eating peanut butter and jelly sandwiches and asking them to pass the milk. And then they would be talking about these problems. My mother would come in and say, “Time to play football.” And everybody would get up and go out. For us kids, it felt like we were part of something bigger.

Your latest book, which has just been published, is a biography of your mother: Ethel Kennedy: The Extraordinary Life and Bold Legacy. What kind of person was she?My mother loved men. If you’re a woman, you’re great, and you’re her friend. But when a man was watching, it was incredible. Her whole life, that’s the way she was. When she was 96 and her mind was kind of in and out, I called her from my hotel in Milan and I mentioned, “I’m here. Can I bring you anything? Do you want some limoncello or a bag of that beautiful spaghetti that they sell at the airport? What can I bring you from Italy?” And she answered, “An Italian boyfriend would be nice.”.

Brandon Armstrong is doing just fine after being accidentally hit by Ezra Frech’s airborne prosthetic leg.

In a Wednesday, November 25, TikTok video posted by his wife, Brylee Armstrong, the Dancing With the Stars pro gave fans a glimpse of a cut on his calf where Frech’s prosthetic injured him during the Paralympian’s freestyle on the season 35 finale the day before.

In a recent development, brandon, 32, was one of the backing dancers during Frech’s freestyle performance with professional partner Daniella Karagach. The routine got off to a rocky start when Frech’s prosthetic leg came off as he jumped onto the stage, but he managed to perform the whole dance and received 10s from all the judges.

Sources indicate that “First of all, fine. Just happy that he’s fine,” Brandon noted of Frech, who won the latest season with Karagach.

He continued, “When he jumped off, his leg was not on properly or all the way, so I took a freaking shot.”.

“It’s actually not too bad. It split me, but it’s not too bad,” Brandon remarked, showing his injury.

The DWTS pro added, “I’m just happy that he is fine. That dance was unbelievable. Leg didn’t get on right, but it got on right the second time, and he killed it, so everything’s good.”.

Judge Derek Hough praised Frech’s expert recovery following the mishap during his freestyle on the Tuesday, November 24, season finale.

“Ezra, you are a hero. This performance will have a ripple effect far beyond this show. What you did tonight … for forever, kids will look up to you and will see what’s possible. The fact that the worst case scenario might have happened and you wouldn’t even have known, the way you rose in that moment,” Hough, 41, said. “Ezra, you are incredible, man!”.

“What we witnessed tonight goes beyond dancing. This is a powerful, beautiful, life-affirming statement that will inspire the nation and the world, my darling,” fellow judge Bruno Tonioli added.

Carrie Ann Inaba mentioned, “You have been the most amazing ambassador for people with disabilities, but also, now you’re an ambassador for dance.”.

The following day on Good Morning America, Frech said he “blacked out” during his freestyle routine.

According to recent reports, “Last night was crazy. … I can’t believe this happened,” Frech, 21, shared. “I can’t believe we got that opportunity to represent [the disabled community].”.

Sources indicate that “We started our freestyle without the prosthetic, that was a creative choice, and then things went a little off script,” Frech said on GMA. “I wasn’t able to suction my leg on and I knew it wasn’t on. Sometimes when that happens, it’ll re-suction, but it didn’t. It came off. She told me to put it on mid-dance, I kinda blacked out.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that "South Park" has been on a roll recently.
  • It's been a funny season, and it's been a heartfelt season at times, particularly when the show killed Kenny (again) and decided to replace him with none other than a kid version of Randy (complete with mustache).
  • Industry observers note that in the finale, "City Endings," the town of South Park (renamed this season as South America) is hit with major power outages that disrupt the town's "GTA VI" gametime.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that "South Park" has been on a roll recently. When the show finally left behind its Mr.-Garrison-as-Trump allegory and stopped doing endless specials (even if most of those were fantastic), it found its stride again in Season 28, which took on AI and deepfakes in the funniest way possible. Then, Season 29 took on everything from the data centers, to "looksmaxxing" and "aura farming" in a hilarious "Backrooms" parody, to club sports in a great "Heated Rivalry" parody, to the US beef shortage, and more.

It's been a funny season, and it's been a heartfelt season at times, particularly when the show killed Kenny (again) and decided to replace him with none other than a kid version of Randy (complete with mustache). It has even been a romantic season, with the Tweek and Craig romance-focused episode. What "South Park" usually isn't, however, is scary. That changed with the Season 29 finale, which delivered the scariest TV scene of 2026 — twice.

Industry observers note that in the finale, "City Endings," the town of South Park (renamed this season as South America) is hit with major power outages that disrupt the town's "GTA VI" gametime. It is part of a conspiracy involving secret deals the government made with billionaire weenies. At the same time, there's paranoia involving supposed Chinese spies and possible cyberattacks from that country.

In the middle of all this, Cartman, Stan, and Kyle are also haunted by visions of the late Kenny, who died after being blown up by an e-bike in the season's premiere. Except this is not just Kenny, but a zombified version that haunts the boys in the form of horrific ghouls that even infiltrate "GTA VI," like a spectre out of "The Ring.".

"South Park" has toyed with the horror genre before, usually body horror. There was the Michael Jackson parody with Mr. Jefferson slowly rotting away, for example, or the HumanCentipad. The Season 29 finale, however, features one of the wildest and most gruesome eldritch abominations in the nearly 30-year history of the show. It starts with several scenes of Kenny simply standing creepily in the background, stalking the boys as if to try and send a message.

In a recent development, "City Endings" is a legit horror episode, which is rare from the show that spent nearly a decade on a silly weed farm storyline. The image of Kenny just standing in the background, his face obscured by his hoodie but with bright eyes just shining like Pennywise in "It," is already quite disturbing and terrifying. Then, when the boys finally catch up to Kenny, who leads them to the cemetery and to his own grave, he highlights off his gruesome zombie face and starts dissolving like that guy in "Poltergeist," in excruciatingly disturbing detail, before exploding in a pool of blood.

Sources indicate that it's enough to make your skin crawl, but it's not even the scariest scene of the episode. That climax comes in later, while the boys are playing "GTA VI" at Butters' house. We see the zombie Kenny monster with long spiky teeth, deranged eyes and elongated limbs with claws crawling out of the TV like Samara Morgan from "The Ring." It is the stuff of pure nightmares, and by far the scariest scene in 2026 television.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the 2017 German sci-fi mystery thriller series Dark aired for three seasons on Netflix, gaining critical acclaim and a global cult following. Its complex plot explored the paradoxical nature of time travel through strange mysteries in the fictional town of Winden, Germany.

Six years after its finale, series creators Baran bo Odar and Jantje Friese are producing a upcoming mystery thriller, Sonnental. HBO Max Germany released a 30-second teaser for the series, introducing the plot and the protagonist played by Dark star Lisa Vicari.

According to recent reports, sonnental shares Dark's spooky atmosphere and eerie woodland setting, but the new series is a crime mystery rather than sci-fi. The plot follows a series of murders based on Der Struwwelpeter, a German book that features 10 stories about misbehaving children whose actions have terrible consequences. In the teaser, we hear the voice of a child singing the first verse of "The Story of Wicked Frederick," the second story in Der Struwwelpeter.

"Der Friederich, der Friederich,.

This translates to "Frederick, Frederick, he was a terrible tyrant." The tale is about a boy who abuses and tortures animals. When a dog Frederick whips bites him, the child becomes ill and bedridden and the dog eats all his food. HBO indicates the book's twisted tales will become "deadly nightmares" in Sonnental, so Frederick's karmic punishment may be even more sinister. All six episodes of Sonnental will premiere on HBO Max in March 2027.

The timing is great for me on this one, taking into account what I personally like to watch. As I mentioned, I cancelled my subscription earlier this fall to save some money, but with Avengers: Doomsday arriving in theaters in a matter of weeks, I'm glad to have access to the various Marvel movies in case I get a hankering to revisit some of them. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, cheat codes have long been a part of the Grand Theft Auto video game franchise, and the tradition continues with GTA 6. Not only does GTA 6 support cheats, but it also has a menu that lists all of them as well as instructions for unlocking them. However, you cannot fire up the game and start using cheats from the beginning. In fact, it requires quite a bit of work on your part. Here's how to unlock cheat codes in GTA 6, how to see the list of cheats, as well as the 10 best cheat codes in GTA 6.

Gone are the good old days when you could fire up GTA, enable god mode, unlimited ammo, no reload, spawn a jetpack, and run around the entire city destroying things at will. In GTA 6, you'll need to complete the main story to unlock the ability to use cheat codes. On top of that, you'll have to complete challenges of various difficulty levels to access specific cheat codes. Some of these cheats unlock the moment you finish the main story. Others, however, are quite challenging or time-consuming. For instance, unlimited reload requires you to win 25 gold medals at shooting ranges.

Recent findings suggest that once you complete the main story in GTA 6, just go to in-game settings, and you'll see a upcoming Cheats tab. This lists all 61 cheats and how to unlock them. You'll see the actual button combo for each cheat right after you complete the unlock requirement.

Recent findings suggest that unfortunately, there are some serious gameplay ramifications to using cheat codes in GTA 6. For starters, you can't save the game once you input even one cheat code. That's why it's best to save before you start using cheats, to avoid losing progress. Using cheat codes will also disable trophies and achievements in GTA 6.

It has been revealed that to start using cheat codes in GTA 6, you'll have to get your character to pull up the smartphone by pressing the up arrow on the D-Pad. Then, hold L1+R1, and press the cheat's key combination on the D-Pad.

While there are a lot of cheat codes in GTA 6, these are 10 of the best, listed with the right key combination, and the condition to unlock them:.

This cheat unlocks the moment you complete the main story in GTA 6. To use it, press up, right, down, left, up, left, down, right.

You unlock this cheat code after losing a three-star wanted level 25 times. The key combination is left, down, right, down, up, down, up.

Lose a three-star wanted level 50 times to unlock this cheat. The key combination is left, down, right, down, up, right, up.

This cheat unlocks the moment you wrap up the main story. Press this to unlock: down, up, up, down, up, down, up, down, up, right.

This is the third cheat that unlocks when you finish the main story. When you shoot or punch/kick characters, this cheat will launch them in the air. The key combination is: down, up, left, right, down, down, up, down.

If you win 25 silver medals at shooting ranges, you can unlock infinite ammo in GTA 6. The key combination is: down, up, right, down, left, left, up, down, down, down.

Recent findings suggest that to stop needing reloads, you need to win 25 gold medals at shooting ranges in GTA 6. The key combination is: down, up, right, down, left, left, up, down, down, up.

Industry observers note that if you complete 100 workouts during your GTA 6 playthrough, you'll unlock the cheat that lets you instantly obtain body armor. Press this key combination to make it work: down, up, left, up, up, up, up, up, down, down.

According to recent reports, this GTA 6 cheat allows you to change the weather at any time, and it unlocks when you finish the main story. Press this key combination to toggle it: down, right, up, down, right, up, right.

To spawn this cool emergency vehicle, you just need to discover the MTL Pumper in the game's progress menu. Use this key combination to spawn one: left, up, right, down, left, left, up, left.

Tech Report: Avengers: Doomsday TV Spot Confirms RDJ's Doctor Doom Has A Scarred Face

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that marvel Comics fans know Doctor Victor von Doom is scarcely ever seen without his iron mask — a mask that hides his supposedly horribly scarred face.
  • In a recent development, now, Chris Evans has claimed that Doom wears his mask for the entirety of "Doomsday." But that could only mean he'll keep the mask on until "Secret Wars." Even then, there's the chance that Doom is so disfigured that his face isn't even recognizable as RDJ.
  • Recent findings suggest that in this TV spot, Magneto (Ian McKellen) tries to telekinetically rip off Doom's mask — it is made of metal, after all.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that marvel Comics fans know Doctor Victor von Doom is scarcely ever seen without his iron mask — a mask that hides his supposedly horribly scarred face. But with Marvel Studios choosing former Tony Stark actor Robert Downey Jr. to play Doom in the upcoming "Avengers" movies "Doomsday" and "Secret Wars," there's been an expectation that Doom's mask coming off will be a jaw dropping moment.

In a recent development, now, Chris Evans has claimed that Doom wears his mask for the entirety of "Doomsday." But that could only mean he'll keep the mask on until "Secret Wars." Even then, there's the chance that Doom is so disfigured that his face isn't even recognizable as RDJ. A fresh TV spot for "Doomsday" does suggest Doom has his scarred face, while also teasing we're eventually going to see exactly what's under his mask ... but not yet.

Recent findings suggest that in this TV spot, Magneto (Ian McKellen) tries to telekinetically rip off Doom's mask — it is made of metal, after all. But Doom does not restrict himself to the laws of science. There's evidently a magical seal on the mask (note there appear to be runic designs across Doom's costume), because glowing green tendrils extend out from Doom's hood and grab the mask, slamming it back onto Doom's face. A brief glimpse of Doom's face, visible through the mask's eyeholes, shows hints of pale macerated skin and scar tissue.

In the "Fantastic Four" comics, it was originally remarked that Doom suffered his scars during an experiment in college. A machine he built to contact the "nether world" (later revealed to be an attempt to reach his mother's damned soul) exploded in his face, leaving him scarred.

It has been revealed that now, Doom's co-creator Jack Kirby intended that Doom actually only had a thin facial scar — but Doom's ego can't stand even that small imperfection. Later "Fantastic Four" writer/artist John Byrne melded the two ideas. The machine explosion only slightly damaged Doom's face, but then Victor — convinced his face was already ruined — put his freshly forged mask on before it cooled, and that is why he has a horribly scarred face.

Recent findings suggest that the greatest source of Doom's torment is completely self-inflicted. The exemplary 1989 "Doctor Strange and Doctor Doom: Triumph and Torment" goes with Byrne's interpretation. When Doom seeks out the wisdom of the wizard named the Aged Genghis, the sorcerer alludes to Doom's "minor disfigurement." We then see Doom's (barely scarred) face as Victor lashes out at the insult.

It has been revealed that it's unclear what origin "Doomsday" will go with, if any of them. Marketing suggests the Marvel Cinematic Universe's Doom will be driven by a lost wife and child, not his mother. What is clear from this TV spot is that Marvel fans can expect to see Doom and Magneto — the two greatest villains of Marvel Comics — clash onscreen. Doom's wizardry here refutes the obvious conclusion that Magneto wins easily because he controls metal and Doom is concealed inside metal armor.

"He is pain, he is extinction," Magneto declares, setting up Doom's famous third person double entendre: "I am Doom!" Ian McKellen's Magneto was the first villain of the Marvel movie boom that kicked off with 2000's "X-Men." Bringing him back to face (and presumably fall to) Doom is some classic carnival barker marketing that would make Stan Lee proud.

"Avengers: Doomsday" is set for theatrical release on December 18, 2026.

21 Best Thanksgiving Movies to Stream This Week

📅 24 Nov 2021 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2100 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vanityfair

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sandwiched between the kitschy horrors of Halloween and the commercialized merriment of Christmas, Thanksgiving is often unfairly overlooked as a cinematic main course.
  • Sources indicate that nevertheless, we’ve collected 21 Thanksgiving movies (and Thanksgiving-adjacent movies) that capture the spirit of the holiday—turkey-trotting, tossing the pigskin, carb-loading, fighting with your family, and then overheating in a gorgeous cashmere sweater.
  • Sources indicate that this isn’t known as the quintessential Thanksgiving movie for nothing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sandwiched between the kitschy horrors of Halloween and the commercialized merriment of Christmas, Thanksgiving is often unfairly overlooked as a cinematic main course. But while there might not be a feast’s worth of Thanksgiving movies, there is undoubtedly an appetite for Thanksgiving fare in film. Look no further than the inclusion of the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade in Miracle on 34th Street or Wednesday Adams’s sinister (if historically-accurate) re-enactment in Addams Family Values for proof that audiences love turkey’s least favorite holiday. Of course, Thanksgiving tends to get a better treatment on TV, inspiring canonical episodes of Gossip Girl, Friends, Master of None, and, of course, A Charlie Brown Thanksgiving.

Sources indicate that nevertheless, we’ve collected 21 Thanksgiving movies (and Thanksgiving-adjacent movies) that capture the spirit of the holiday—turkey-trotting, tossing the pigskin, carb-loading, fighting with your family, and then overheating in a gorgeous cashmere sweater. Here’s to finding post-meal common ground with one of the titles on this list.

Sources indicate that this isn’t known as the quintessential Thanksgiving movie for nothing. You know the story: Steve Martin’s uptight marketing executive, Neal, just wants to travel from New York to Chicago for turkey with his family. His plans for an uneventful trip are foiled again and again by John Candy’s boisterous shower-ring salesman, Del, who’s eager to make friends with Neal during their wayward journey. We will never look at pillows—or rental car agents—the same way again.

In a recent development, don’t let the word Christmas in the title scare you away. This 2016 ensemble comedy starring Danny Glover, Kimberly Elise, Mo’Nique, and Gabrielle Union has undeniable Thanksgiving vibes. Produced by Will Packer and originally sold to Universal Pictures under the title A Meyers Thanksgiving, Almost Christmas follows the dysfunctional Meyers family as the family patriarch, Walter Meyers (Glover), tries to get through his first holiday season after the death of his wife. While it isn’t exactly about Thanksgiving per se, most of the best moments in Almost Christmas—including Elise chasing Romany Malco away from the table with a shotgun, or the whole table having to pretend to like Mo’Nique’s terrible food—take place during large family gatherings around the dinner table. What could be more Thanksgiving-coded than that? With an all-star cast of Black actors that also includes J.B. Smoove, Nicole Ari Parker, Omar Epps, and Gladys Knight, Almost Christmas feels like a homecoming full of your favorite uncles and aunties. And, to be fair, isn’t Thanksgiving almost Christmas?

Sources indicate that the turkey isn’t the only thing getting carved up in this holiday slasher. Starring Patrick Dempsey and Tik Toker turned recording artist turned film actress Addison Rae, Thanksgiving begins with a Black Friday sale gone horribly awry in Plymouth, Massachusetts, leading to the death of multiple customers. The following year, a murderous slasher wearing a John Carver mask is wreaking havoc in Plymouth, and targeting Rae’s Gaby and her friends. If you’re not feeling warm and gooey on over the holiday, you might want to throw on Thanksgiving and watch Rae and Dempsey’s Sheriff Eric Newton try and track down and escape the clutches of a grisly murderer.

In Jodie Foster’s comedy, Holly Hunter plays Claudia Larson, who returns home for Thanksgiving after losing her job and learning that her daughter (My So-Called Life–era Claire Danes) aims to spend the holiday with a boyfriend. The family she returns to is filled with colorful performances from Anne Bancroft and Charles Durning as her eclectic parents, Robert Downey Jr. as her misanthrope brother, and Dylan McDermott as a semi-mysterious dinner guest.

Fantastic Mr. Fox isn’t technically about Thanksgiving, or even really about humans. And yet, Wes Anderson’s 2009 stop-motion film, featuring the voices of George Clooney and Meryl Streep, has been labeled a Thanksgiving must-watch. Perhaps that’s because the film, based on Roald Dahl’s classic children’s novel, is all about animals trying to escape the tyranny of farmers—something every turkey not lucky enough to be pardoned by the president wishes it could do around Thanksgiving time. Beyond the war between animals and farmers, Anderson’s rustic color palette filled with burnt orange—and the massive feast that brings a diverse array of animals around a dinner table after they successfully joined forces to steal food from their nemeses—are full of the spirit of Thanksgiving.

According to recent reports, at times, the titular April’s (Katie Holmes) fate feels as if it rests on whether she’ll successfully cook a turkey in her crowded Lower East Side apartment. As April prepares to host her suburban Pennsylvania family, the high-stakes nature of spending a day hunkered down with relatives—played by Patricia Clarkson, Oliver Platt, Alison Pill, and John Gallagher Jr.—rushes in.

In a recent development, sometimes getting families together over the holidays is fraught. In this 1997 moody drama directed by Ang Lee, two affluent Connecticut families unravel over Thanksgiving break as their secrets come to lights. The ensemble cast includes stalwart actors Kevin Kline, Joan Allen, Sigourney Weaver as messy parents, and, at that point, up and comers, Tobey Maguire, Elijah Wood, and Christina Ricci as their even more troubled teens. The Ice Storm, which won best screenplay at Cannes Film Festival, is rife with adultery, substance abuse, as well as surprising turns from a host of talented actors and a sharp early film from one of cinema’s most celebrated directors.

Nothing feels more nostalgic during Thanksgiving than watching Snoopy whip up a makeshift meal with jelly beans, popcorn, and mountains of buttered toast for all of his Peanuts pals. And Vince Guraldi’s timeless score makes for a perfect soundtrack to your own festivities.

Industry observers note that A Thanksgiving flashback provides key context for the complicated dynamics amongst this group of recently-reunited college friends, played by Glenn Close, Kevin Kline, Jeff Goldblum, Mary Kay Place, and William Hurt. Lawrence Kasdan’s film earned three Oscar nominations, including best picture, original screenplay, and supporting actress for Close.

While not a Thanksgiving-themed film, protagonist Nola Darling (Tracy Camilla Johns) invites all three of her potential suitors to a tense dinner on that very holiday, making her memorable decision between them from her head-of-the-table vantage point. This was most of the world’s introduction to Spike Lee, both as an actor and director, and the electricity is still palpable. And if you’ve gotta have more? You can always stream the 2017 Netflix original series of the same name, starring Lee and DeWanda Wise as Nola Darling.

Sources indicate that rian Johnson’s whodunnit has all the trappings of a Thanksgiving movie, without ever mentioning the holiday. There’s family infighting, Chris Evans in a cable-knit sweater, foggy fall weather, and even a political allegory about the treatment of people of color. Also not about Thanksgiving, but worthy viewing for the full family: Glass Onion: A Knives Out Mystery, which hit theaters last November.

The same year that Merriam-Webster acknowledged Instagram captions everywhere by adding “Friendsgiving” to the dictionary, a movie of the same name was released. True to its titular tradition, a group of friends convenes for a meal that inevitably devolves into chaos.

While not an outright Thanksgiving movie, 1997’s ensemble dramedy contains some of the most sumptuous shots of food ever committed to film. After the death of their family matriarch, a group of disparate relatives must put aside their differences and reconvene for a weekly Sunday dinner. Starring Vivica A. Fox, Vanessa Williams, and Nia Long, Soul Food captures the bonding powers that plates of cornbread, catfish, and collard greens can bring.

In a recent development, this 1976 best picture Oscar winner stars Sylvester Stallone as the eponymous down-on-his-luck boxer, whose fate begins to change with the meeting of his future wife, Adrian (Talia Shire). “To you, it’s Thanksgiving. To me, it’s Thursday,” Rocky tells Adrian as he whisks her away from a disastrous family feast minutes after her brother Paulie (Burt Young) hurls her turkey into the nearby alley. As fans of the franchise, which has debuted several films over the Thanksgiving holiday, know, their Thanksgiving meet-cute will stand the test of time.

Thanksgiving isn’t always about bickering with your blood relatives. Spend Thanksgiving with Instant Family, which stars Mark Wahlberg and Rose Byrne as Pete and Ellie Wagner, an unwitting couple who, overnight, become parents to three foster children. Their decision to become parents happens over  a tense Thanksgiving dinner where Ellie’s family shares they don’t think that Pete and Ellie were ever really cut out to be parents. In an effort to prove them wrong, the Wagners wind up biting off more than they bargained for as they become foster parents to three children, the eldest played by Madame Web star Isabela Merced.

Before Greta Gerwig forced Noah Baumbach to write Barbie with her, there was Mistress America. Written by the real-life couple who helmed the billion dollar blockbuster, this 2015 Sundance favorite centers on the unlikely friendship between Lola Kirke’s Tracy, a first-year college student alone in New York, and Gerwig’s Brooke, the Times Square-living twentysomething who will soon become her stepsister. Conflict between the pair gets resolved on Thanksgiving at New York City’s Veselka, a Ukrainian institution where pierogis stand in for the traditional bird.

Greta Gerwig must really love Thanksgiving. The auteur’s Oscar-nominated take on the Louisa May Alcott classic is brimming with cozy, Thanksgiving-esque vibes. Set largely in the weeks before Christmas, the March sisters (Saoirse Ronan, Emma Watson, Eliza Scanlen, and Florence Pugh) and matriarch (Laura Dern) battle wits, trot through the snow, and stage living room plays in a film that feels reminiscent of many a-family gatherings.

“First, let’s give thanks to our families not being here. It’s always easier without the family,” Adam Sandler’s George Simmons, a stand-up comedian who has been newly diagnosed with cancer, indicates to a group of new friends. In Judd Apatow’s 2009 dramedy, George attempts to revamp his fledgling career in the eleventh hour with the help of aspiring comic Ira Wright (Seth Rogen). At one point, he  joins the younger talent’s friendsgiving festivities, where the table is surrounded by stars including Jonah Hill, Jason Schwartzman, Aubrey Plaza, and Bo Burnham.

Industry observers note that in one of the newer entries to the turkey day canon, Stephen Karam adapts his 2015 Pulitzer finalist play of the same name, exploring the long-held resentments and deeply-rooted admiration that live in an East Coast family. Jayne Houdyshell reprises her Tony-winning role as Deirdre alongside a stacked ensemble, including Richard Jenkins, June Squibb, Beanie Feldstein, Steven Yeun, and Amy Schumer, all gathered in a drab Chinatown apartment for Thanksgiving.

Industry observers note that prisoners finds Hugh Jackman and Jake Gyllenhaal teaming up to find a pair of missing girls who were abducted after Thanksgiving dinner in Conyers, Pennsylvania. EGOT recipient Viola Davis also stars in the thriller as the mother of one of the kidnapped girls. Directed by Dune’s Denis Villeneuve, Prisoners is an unconventional and unsettling Thanksgiving film.

Another unconventional choice, Sam Raimi’s Spider-Man is arguably the only superhero movie that doubles as a Thanksgiving movie. While the central action follows Tobey Maguire’s Peter Parker, there’s a pivotal scene set at Thanksgiving dinner that directly follows a heated battle between Spider-Man and the Green Goblin (a.k.a Norman Osborne, played by Willem Dafoe.) Parker and Osborne have Thanksgiving dinner together with MJ (Kirsten Dunst), Harry Osborne (James Franco), and Aunt May (Rosemary Harris). During the meal, Osborne comes to the stunning realization that Peter Parker is, in fact, Spider-Man. Others have already made the case that the first Spider-Man film deserves to be included in the Thanksgiving canon. The way Dafoe carves the turkey is also both sinister and iconic, as is Maguire apologizing for his tardiness because he “had to beat an old lady with a stick to get these cranberries.”.

Support for storing your driver’s license in Apple Wallet has gradually been expanding across the United States. Today, we have a status update on when the feature will go live in Connecticut, which Apple has touted as a planned partner since September 2021.

According to recent reports, 9to5Mac is sponsored by Sony: Score Sony’s INZONE noise-canceling earbuds for 38% off. These deliver immersive 360 Spatial Sound, active noise canceling, low-latency wireless connectivity, and much more.

According to recent reports, last week, Connecticut released its own mobile ID app for iPhone on the App Store, but without Apple Wallet support. As spotted by MacRumors, however, the app’s developer indicates that Apple Wallet support is “coming soon.”.

Industry observers note that connecticut residents have been waiting a long time for the state to launch Apple Wallet ID support. This is the first notable update we’ve had in a while.

When Apple announced support for storing your driver’s license in Apple Wallet in 2021, the organization touted the following partners:.

Evidence found within Apple’s backend code suggests that Utah support should go live soon.

Recent findings suggest that you can use Apple Wallet IDs at TSA checkpoints, as well as at select businesses and organizations in person, in app, and online. It does not replace your physical license. Here are the full details on acceptance.

Here’s how this year's “buy one, get one” (BOGO) deal works: Pick out a starter kit from one of the brands, add it to your cart, and you’ll be presented with a list of available tools you can add (they’ll be marked “FREE,” so you can’t get confused). When you go to check out, the price of the tool will be listed as “SAVINGS.”.

Here are the starter kits you can choose from:.

In a recent development, ryobi ONE+ 18V Starter Kit (includes one 4.0Ah and one 2.0Ah battery and charger). Cost: $99.

Recent findings suggest that deWalt 20V Max Starter Kit (includes 6.0Ah and 4.0Ah batteries and charger). Cost: $199.

In a recent development, makita 18V LXT Starter Pack (includes two 5.0Ah batteries and a rapid charger). Cost: $199.

In a recent development, milwaukee M18 FUEL Combo Kit (includes a brushless, cordless hammer drill and an impact driver). Cost: $399.

Note that the Ryobi, DeWalt, and Milwaukee offers include 14 free tools to choose from, while the Makita offer only includes 8. Also, note that while the Ryobi starter kit is your cheapest option for a free tool, the batteries included are weaker. For example, if you choose the DeWalt Starter Kit for $199, you can get an Atomic 20V Max impact wrench that normally costs $239 for free, which is a significant savings even if you already have batteries and a charger and don’t really need those items (plus, you can never have too many batteries).

The Home Depot is also offering deep discounts on just about everything in the store. Some of the most notable tool deals include:.

50% off this DeWalt Cordless Brushless Oscillating Multi Tool, including battery and charger.

33% off this Ryobi Combo Kit, an incredible deal for a circular saw, reciprocating saw, and a power drill/driver plus two batteries and a charger; the batteries are small, but this is a great deal on a starter kit.

42% off this Combo Kit from Milwaukee, including a Packout toolbox, a hammer drill, an impact driver, a grinder, and a reciprocating saw, plus two batteries and a charger—a massive deal for anyone who needs to tool up rapidly.

45% off this Brushless Cordless Impact Wrench Kit from Ryobi, which includes a battery and charger.

That only scratches the surface—if you’ve ever needed anything from Home Depot, Black Friday is the day to run out and get it.

Of course, Black Friday can be a little chaotic, so here are a few tips to maximize your savings and experience:.

Sources indicate that check online and in-store. Some deals are in-store only, and some items (especially BOGO tools) may not be available at your nearest location—make sure you enter your ZIP code when you’re checking out to ensure you won’t have any problems.

Recent findings suggest that consider whether you need more batteries and chargers. Depending on your existing collection of batteries and chargers, buying more to get the discount may or may not make sense.

There's no price matching or rain checks. Remember that the store won’t honor price-matching or offer rain checks on Black Friday items.

Cyber Monday will have deals, too. More deals will be rolled out on Cyber Monday (November 30), which may include items you want but don’t see on sale for Black Friday. But keep in mind that Black Friday prices probably won’t go any lower—so snap up what you need as soon as you can.

Industry observers note that the best prices of the year on tools are during the holidays in November and December. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that prime Video has been serving up a feast for romantic comedy fans in 2026.
  • The film is called "Clashing Through the Snow" and before you immediately close this window just let me explain.
  • Sources indicate that until recently, Nicolas Cage and Christian Bale's sports movie "Madden" was topping the Prime Video charts.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that prime Video has been serving up a feast for romantic comedy fans in 2026. Lili Reinhart's rom-com "The Love Hypothesis" just finished dominating the Prime Video charts, which came in the wake of Ester Expósito's romantic thriller "Drawn Together" becoming a Prime streaming hit. Now, the streamer has added a Christmas-themed romance just in time for the holidays, and this one stars "Landman" actor Michelle Randolph.

The film is called "Clashing Through the Snow" and before you immediately close this window just let me explain. Yes, the name sounds like the result of a "give me a cheesy Christmas rom-com title" ChatGPT prompt, but Randolph alone should pique your interest. The actor has quietly been delivering standout performances in Taylor Sheridan's "Landman" and his "Yellowstone" prequel "1923." The former sees her play Ainsley Norris, the ditzy but determined daughter of Billy Bob Thornton's oil man Tommy Norris. Based on her performances in those shows, Randolph surely has a bright future ahead. While "Clashing Through the Snow" might not be her major breakthrough, it's doing pretty darn well on Prime Video.

Sources indicate that until recently, Nicolas Cage and Christian Bale's sports movie "Madden" was topping the Prime Video charts. But it's now been knocked out of the top spot by this festive romance movie, in which publishing editor Hannah Hendricks (Randolph) is forced to take a road trip with her rival, Ryan Mitchell (Chris Briney). You can see where this is going.

According to streaming viewership tracker FlixPatrol, the film has now hit number two on the United States overall Prime Video chart (which combines TV and films) as of Thanksgiving day, and sits at number one on the movie chart. But Michelle Randolph's comedy is proving popular elsewhere, too. In fact, it's become a global hit. At the time of writing, the film is charting on 61 countries' top 10 movie rankings, which is a pretty good showing. Even more impressive, "Clashing Through the Snow" is number one on the movie charts in 47 of those countries, including the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom.

Meanwhile, the movie has managed to break into the overall chart in 30 countries, taking the top spot in five of them. That means "Clashing Through the Snow" is the most-watched piece of media on Prime Video in Austria, Poland, Portugal, South Africa, and Switzerland. It even managed to hit number one on the overall chart in the U.S. on November 25, 2026. That's a notable achievement, as often films will break into the top 10 movies without making it onto the overall charts. "Clashing Through the Snow" must be good, then...

"Clashing Through the Snow" is a comfortingly familiar rom-com outing that's perfect for the holidays. The film sees Chris Briney's Ryan Mitchell and Michelle Randolph's Hannah Hendricks stranded at an airport during a snowstorm, after which they share a rental car and set out on a cross-country trip to Latest York. The pair both need to close a deal in order to save their jobs — but wouldn't you know it, they fall in love instead. Along the way there's plenty of romantic Christmas movie moments as the couple stop in charming small towns and overcome mishaps together. Is "Clashing Through the Snow" pushing the boundaries of rom-coms? No. Is it charming? Sure is.

The film is directed by Carlson Young, who made her feature directorial debut with the 2021 fantasy horror "The Blazing World" before directing Sophie Turner in 2025's "Trust." She also oversaw a couple of Prime Video rom-coms before "Clashing Through the Snow," directing 2024's "Upgraded" and 2026's "The Last Sunrise.".

Sources indicate that now, she's delivered a major hit with her Randolph-led Christmas rom-com, which has a 77% audience score on Rotten Tomatoes. There aren't enough reviews to earn it a critic score yet, but while William Bibbiani of TheWrap found it to be "unapologetically clichéd" he also found the dialogue to be memorable and saw the film as "an efficient delivery mechanism for semi-believable rom and semi-funny com.".

If that sounds appealing, "Clashing Through the Snow" is streaming on Prime Video right now.

In a recent development, one person who has been the talk of the town in the world of celebrity fashion is Julianne Hough. As Dancing with the Stars aired its 35th season on the 2026 TV schedule, she made some very bold outfit choices, and in response, fans did not hold back their opinions on them. Now, her stylist has spoken out about the critical discourse regarding the co-host’s DWTS ensembles.

I’ll be the first to admit that when Julianne Hough walked into the ballroom for a given episode of DWTS, I was often shocked by her outfits. They were bold, sometimes avant-garde and always fun to see. According to her stylist, Brad Goreski, they were trying going for fits that were “super elevated and strong” as well as “super extravagant and wild and playful and colorful and sparkly.” I think they achieved that goal, as you can see in the photos of Hough and her co-host Alfonso Ribeiro below:.

Image credit: Disney/Eric McCandless.

Image credit: Disney/Christopher Willard.

The co-host’s fashion choices throughout the season (which you can see with a Disney+ subscription) led to quite a bit of criticism from fans. One person posted one of Hough’s sheer outfits on Instagram and wrote over it, “Respectfully, who is Julianne’s stylist and why do they need to be fired?” Meanwhile, someone on X remarked they thought the people dressing Hough were “playing a cruel joke” on her. These kinds of comments happened week after week.

When Goreski and Hough spoke to Glamour about her style this season, they addressed the backlash that came with it too. The dancer’s stylist stated he has “an awareness” of it. He also explained:.

In a recent development, and I love it. Any conversation, good or bad, around fashion is great. I think people weighing in—they like the hair but not the dress; they thought it was a bad outfit; they think she should fire me—is totally fine, because we’re really excited by what we’re doing, and we put a lot of thought and energy into it. I think Jules ultimately brings the looks to life, and I’m glad that there’s another part of the show that people talk about. Not every person’s going to love every look. I know that from being a stylist for 15 years. And that’s okay.

According to recent reports, well, that’s certainly a good mentality to have about all this. Along with that, Hough noted that evolving her style came with risk too. Millions of people watch DWTS, and as her stylist explained, not everyone will like her looks. So, with that being remarked, the co-host stated that her motto this season was “apathy is the enemy.” She also had this to say about how people react to her fashion choices:.

According to recent reports, the reason things exist and have charge and stay visible [is] people either love it or hate it. They still want to talk about it.

Sources indicate that to that point, there were lots of moments on DWTS this year that got people on the internet talking, like liftgate, Jennifer Lawrence trolling Connor Wood, and Ezra Frech making it through his freestyle after his prosthetic fell off. Overall, Season 35 was met with a whole lot of love, but also quite a bit of intense discourse too. And yes, part of that had to do with Julianne Hough's fashion choices.

However, as both the co-host and her stylist noted, part of the fun of fashion is getting people talking about it.

PS5s Are in Short Supply for Black Friday, but You Can Still Buy One

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There may be a ton of Black Friday deals on electronics, toys, and gadgets out there, but don't get your hopes up if you're looking for a PlayStation 5.
  • Industry observers note that whether you're looking for a PlayStation 5 Digital Edition, a PS5 with a disc drive, or the flagship PlayStation 5 Pro, you won't find them at major online retailers.
  • You still have some options for obtaining a PS5, but none of them are great.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There may be a ton of Black Friday deals on electronics, toys, and gadgets out there, but don't get your hopes up if you're looking for a PlayStation 5. Not only are they not discounted, but the combination of international chip shortages, high demand caused by the release of Grand Theft Auto 6, and the general holiday shopping frenzy has also made it nearly impossible to purchase a newly introduced, unbundled PlayStation 5 at any price—nearly impossible, but not impossible.

Industry observers note that whether you're looking for a PlayStation 5 Digital Edition, a PS5 with a disc drive, or the flagship PlayStation 5 Pro, you won't find them at major online retailers. PlayStation Direct lists all three consoles as "right now unavailable." Best Buy suggests making an account with them to "improve your odds" of getting one. I can't find a listing for a new PS5 on Amazon either.

You still have some options for obtaining a PS5, but none of them are great. Many refurbished PS5s are selling for well above the list price of a fresh unit. There are some bundled, special editions available, but you'll likely be paying a ton for those. If you're willing to get your hands dirty by dealing with the wild west of Facebook Marketplace, you might be able to track down a used PlayStation 5 at a reasonable price, but approach with extreme caution.

Recent findings suggest that if you're looking for a refurbished PlayStation 5, the best way to avoid a headache is to focus on who did the refurbishing. Buying refurbished electronics directly from a manufacturer is generally safer than buying from a third party, and in this case, it's cheaper too. PlayStation Direct is offering a "Certified Refurbished PlayStation 5 Console" for the relatively reasonable price of $519, while a refurbished Slim sells for $499. But if you're in the market, I'd lock it in quick: PlayStation Direct is already out of refurbished PS5 Pros.

Recent findings suggest that amazon's Renewed program has some strict requirements for third parties to stay in the program, like keeping defect rates under 0.8%, but refurbished PlayStation 5s are going for a premium on Amazon at the moment. A quick look at the site reveals that the price of a refurbished PlayStation 5 is hovering near $900; a refurbished PS5 Slim will run you somewhere around $750, and the current average price of a refurbished PS5 Pro has ballooned to over $1,700. These are well above the retail prices of $649 for the standard version, $599 for the digital version, and $899 for the flagship Pro version of the PlayStation 5.

Industry observers note that there are some bundled versions of the console listed for sale online too. If you buy one of these, you're getting a latest console and some other piece of hardware or a game, but there's a ton of upcharge at the moment. They're generally more expensive than the original price and more expensive than refurbished units as well. Here are some examples:.

Best Buy lists this PS5 Pro with PlayStation Portal Remote for $2,134.99.

GameStop lists a Ghost of Yotei Gold Limited Edition PS5 bundle for $769.99 ($731.49 for GameStop Pros).

Best Buy lists a PS5 Slim with an external drive for $979.99.

According to recent reports, by far the largest used market for anything in the U.S. is Facebook Marketplace, including PlayStation 5s. I checked out my local Marketplace, and there are a lot of listings for the console within a 40-mile radius of Los Angeles. The average price of used PS5 consoles here is hovering between $300 and $500, which seems fairly reasonable. But with Facebook Marketplace, the number of potential red flags rises with the demand for the product.

Industry observers note that I've bought and sold a fair number of things on Marketplace with no problems beyond the occasional flaky person, and I've written a list of hacks for the service, but I wasn't covering a "shortage buying" situation like this. Scams tend to rise with demand, so when I see a listing for a $150 PS5 console (that contains the text "$250 or best offer"), I'm suspicious. It could have been posted by someone who doesn't know what they have, but I wouldn't count on it. If you're buying a PS5 on Marketplace, check the model and generation details very carefully against the actual item. Make sure the seller is offering what you want and not a PlayStation 4 with PS5 games. Verify how it was stored and the condition it's in. But it ultimately can come down to vibes: Don't let your desire to score a PlayStation 5 get in the way of your gut check about the seller or situation.

According to recent reports, in short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Industry observers note that follow our Black Friday coverage for the latest and best deals our team finds. Another good tip is to only buy what you need. It sounds simple, but making a list of the things you want before jumping into a sale with millions of products helps you focus and make smarter decisions.
