📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

[Editor’s note: The following story contains minor spoilers for “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth.”].

Sources indicate that A few years ago, Quentin Tarantino was set to direct one last movie to fulfill his self-imposed ten film limit before riding off into the sunset. And while he was open about his desire to stay creative in other mediums, not even the most outside-the-box thinkers would have predicted that his next massive screen project would be a Netflix movie he wrote for David Fincher. “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” is an unlikely miracle that emerged for a few distinct reasons: Tarantino’s hesitance to commit to his final directing effort, Brad Pitt‘s determination to play Cliff Booth again and his longtime friendship with David Fincher, and of course, the collapse of Tarantino’s planned film “The Movie Critic.” Related Stories How Disney’s ‘Hexed’ Reinvents the Witch Through Animation Robert Aramayo’s Star-Making Turn in ‘I Swear’ Is Already Award-Winning, Now He Just Wants People to See It.

Recent findings suggest that given that “The Movie Critic” was also reportedly set in 1970s Los Angeles, and Pitt had signed on to reprise his “Once Upon a Time in Hollywood” role, there was always going to be speculation about that script turning into “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth.” Tarantino pours gasoline on that flame in the new film when Karen Crosby (Elizabeth Debicki), the Hollywood manager who serves as both a foil and love interest to Booth, reveals that she used to be a film critic before moving into talent representation. The revelation is not crucial to the plot, though it does provide some clever character development as she explains her view that all movies are the culinary equivalent of hamburgers: enjoyable, but not worthy of serious analysis. Yet the inclusion of those lines kicked off a treasure hunt for fans of a director whose unmade movies are almost as legendary as the ones he actually shot.

Recent findings suggest that A definitive answer to the question of “How much of ‘The Movie Critic’ made it into ‘Cliff Booth?'” is going to be hard to come by. Tarantino scripts are some of the most closely guarded secrets in Hollywood, and even the attached actors are often kept in the dark about scenes that don’t concern them. (In an interview with IndieWire, Debicki denied knowing anything about “The Movie Critic,” and everything we know about Tarantino’s process suggests that she was telling the truth.) Beyond that, reports about “The Movie Critic” suggest that the project was constantly changing, even as it neared the planned start of production. It’s impossible to know about every iteration of the project that may have existed at one point or another, but we can use the history of on-the-record quotes and credible reporting about “The Movie Critic” to make an educated guess about where it ended and “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” began.

Cinephiles spent much of 2023 and 2024 receiving piecemeal updates on what was supposed to be Tarantino’s farewell effort. When the project was first reported in March 2023, all we had was the title and a rumor that it was based on legendary New Yorker film critic Pauline Kael. But two months later, Tarantino began to reveal plot details that suggested it was actually inspired by an unnamed film critic who wrote for a magazine he stocked in the porn theaters that he used to work at.

In a recent development, “All the other stuff was too skanky to read, but then there was this porno rag that had a really interesting movie page,” Tarantino stated in a May 2025 interview with Deadline. “He wrote about mainstream movies, and he was the second-string critic. I think he was a very good critic. He was as cynical as hell. His reviews were a cross between early Howard Stern and what Travis Bickle might be if he were a film critic. Think about Travis’ diary entries.”.

According to recent reports, tarantino went on to say that the movie would take place in Los Angeles in 1977 (just like “Cliff Booth” eventually does) and would take inspiration from the critic’s real life, though the porno rag he wrote for would be fictionalized as The Popstar Pages. The director explained that he had done research on the largely unknown writer’s life, saying that “He wrote like he was 55 but he was only in his early to mid-30s. He died in his late thirties. It wasn’t clear for a while but now I’ve done some more research and I think it was complications due to alcoholism.” He also added that the role would have gone to an American man in his mid-30s, with rumors that Paul Walter Hauser was up for the part.

Sources indicate that tarantino noted that the film, which was set up with his “Once Upon a Time in Hollywood” backers at Sony, was set to begin “pre-pre-production” in June 2023, and the film secured a California tax credit to shoot the following year. But by April 2024, Tarantino officially scrapped the project. A blockbuster report in THR detailed the many creative changes that “The Movie Critic” went through during its tumultuous year of pre-production. Pitt’s involvement was never in doubt, but the report says that Tarantino looked at multiple ways of incorporating stars of his previous films like John Travolta and Jamie Foxx. He reportedly considered introducing the concept that his movies like “Pulp Fiction” and “Django Unchained” were real ’70s films that existed in this universe, possibly shooting new sequences from movies-within-movies or having his stars show up as the actors who played those characters. There was also an idea that they would interact with a teenage movie theater usher who would be a Sammy Fabelman-style stand-in for a young Tarantino.

Industry observers note that none of which happens in “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth.” Debicki’s character claims that she wrote movie reviews for a grocery store circular, not a porno rag, and she has far more Pauline Kael than Travis Bickle or Howard Stern in her. And it’s hard to imagine that her and Hauser are ever up for the same parts. The only returning Tarantino characters are Booth and Margot Robbie’s Sharon Tate, who appears in a commercial for his signature fake brand Red Apple Cigarettes. But it’s not hard to see how this film could have emerged from the ashes of that one.

Industry observers note that when you put all of the reporting about “The Movie Critic” together, it appears that the only constants were Tarantino’s desire to revisit the vintage L.A. world of “Once Upon a Time in Hollywood,” bring back Cliff Booth, and illustrate how working in a movie theater and watching ’70s cinema shaped his worldview and his future. The project collapsed because he couldn’t settle on a story that would incorporate all of those elements while containing enough gravity to serve as his directorial mic drop. But regardless of how many specific plot details from “The Movie Critic” survived the transition to “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth,” all of those elements are present in the movie opening this week.

The film opens with a movie-within-a-movie, a fictional blaxploitation effort starring Yahya Abdul-Mateen II. From there, we see that Cliff is working as a projectionist at the New Beverly Cinema, where he also conducts some of his shadier business after hours. He does tell two of his teenage concession stand workers that their young age means it’s time to clock out — if you squint hard enough, that might be considered an Easter Egg about Tarantino’s youth and his possible inclusion in “The Movie Critic,” but the brief encounter hardly makes them seem like stand-ins for a man who loves to memorialize himself.

Sources indicate that in a recent interview with Empire, Fincher remarked that he and Pitt each played a role in cutting 60 pages from the 230-page script that Tarantino initially turned in, resulting in a movie that took place in his sprawling world but was shaped by the type of movie that his two collaborators wanted to make. Looking through that lens, a plausible story for how one movie turned into another begins to take shape.

If you believe all of the reporting, it seems clear enough that Tarantino scrapped “The Movie Critic” because he had more vibes than plot. And “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” provides those exact vibes in droves. We’ll never be able to truly know how many elements were carried over unless Tarantino ever releases or novelizes his “Movie Critic” script (and even then, we won’t be able to fully trust that he didn’t make changes over the subsequent years.) But the safest guess is that he took the idea of Brad Pitt wandering through a darker, sleazier version of L.A. than the hippie paradise he inhabited a decade earlier and simply replaced the intends to make a grand statement about cinema with a pulpy crime plot that could have been ripped from one of his beloved Elmore Leonard novels. And the film still devotes plenty of time to showing scenes from fictional ’70s movies and TV shows, so Tarantino still had a chance to indulge that impulse.

Recent findings suggest that the only other factor that can’t be dismissed is the possibility of self-referential trolling. Tarantino might love talking about movies more than he loves watching them. His insistence on retiring after ten films has nothing to do with his own enjoyment of the filmmaking process — in his own words, he simply doesn’t want anyone studying his future filmography to declare that he got washed up at the end of his career. Anyone who factors the opinions of future podcasters into his own major life decisions is deeply aware of what people say about him, and it’s possible that he simply included the lines about Karen’s career as a critic to add to the mythology about one of his legendary unmade movies. For all we know, the fact that IndieWire published this essay and you read it could be the exact reaction he wanted. In that case, well played, Mr. Tarantino.

Recent findings suggest that “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” is now playing in IMAX theaters. It will be available to stream on Netflix starting Wednesday, December 23.

The iconic YouTube app icon that looked like a retro TV found on iOS might be making a comeback, with new customizable icons showing up behind the scenes of a new YouTube update.

In the early days of the iPhone, Apple built a custom app for YouTube on iOS before Google built its own. That included an app icon that looked like a retro TV and it was later replaced when YouTube’s official app launched on the platform.

Now, that icon might be coming back.

In a recent development, android Authority spotted several new app icons YouTube for Android is testing in its latest beta upgrade (v21.47.483-BETA). These icons seem to be tied to a new feature that would allow consumers to customize the homescreen icon for YouTube, and includes seven designs in total including two throwback designs. One is the aforementioned retro TV icon used on iOS, which was never on YouTube for Android, and another is an old stacked YouTube logo design.

That noted, it’s very fun to get these throwbacks, and we’ll be excited to see this functionality go live.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that amid all the sex and murder in “The Hunting Wives” Season 2 — and there is a lot of sex and murder — the riskiest scene suspends itself between the two. Sophie (Brittany Snow), an East Coast liberal out of place in the conservative Texas town of Maple Brook, and Margo (Malin Åkerman), the mysterious local matriarch who can wrap just about anyone around her finely manicured fingertips, are confronted with a fresh dilemma. For spoilers sake, I won’t get into specifics, but the issue is urgent and impacts them both, without being serious enough to warrant what turns out to be their first-thought fix:.

According to recent reports, in the moment, their lethal instinct seems reasonable. Margo already shot a pregnant teenager in the woods, and Sophie committed vehicular homicide against Margo’s brother (which invited suspicions about Sophie’s past, considering its eerie similarities to a deadly “accident” back in Massachusetts). Their friends, neighbors, and even a youth pastor met their maker, too — just in the first season! So what’s one more body to bury? Go on! Kill ’em! Get yours! Related Stories ‘The Lowdown’ Season 2 Finale Hinges on Two Monologues — Let Ethan Hawke and Sterlin Harjo Break Them Down Will Ferrell Golf Comedy ‘The Hawk’ Canceled at Netflix After Just One Season.

It has been revealed that but before their bloodlust gets the best of them, their better angels make one last plea. Margo hesitates. Sophie follows suit. The gears start turning as they stare into each other’s wide, worried eyes: Are they really prepared to take another life? Are people that disposable to them? What does their initial response say about how they’ve changed? What does it mean about who they’ve become?

Sources indicate that no need to spoil what happens next. The pause makes all the difference. “The Hunting Wives” has always been self-aware, but Margo and Sophie’s recognition of slaughter as their default response to trouble is a critical moment in a second season that reloads without slowing down. Creator Rebecca Cutler knows her Netflix soap is careening past the point where its central couple can reasonably return to lives lived between Margarita Mondays and Sunday church. Killing again, so quickly and carelessly, puts them on the precipice of becoming Bonnie and Clyde Bonnie — known fugitives who are only out for each other. Taking a beat lends the series a critical perspective — a vantage point from the top of the roller coaster, right before the big drop, where you can appreciate for a few brief, fleeting seconds the insanity to come.

Recent findings suggest that then you’re flying. You (and Margo and Sophie) are convinced it’s better to just move forward. Heck, this crisis isn’t going to fix itself!

According to recent reports, margo and Sophie’s breakneck pace to break necks is mostly a feature in Netflix’s surprise hit. The high-key camp comedy and low-key conservative satire moves swiftly, sure, but where its characters are often flustered and panicked, it’s decisive in a way that exudes confidence. Progress is fast but assured. The drama is elevated but mindful. Characters don’t ask for permission or forgiveness; they just go after what they want, what they need, or what they feel they have to have, creating a propulsive viewing experience that zips by in a (muzzle) flash.

It’s a welcome change from prestige dramas that regularly feel like they’re stalling for time. While other demonstrates tout firearms around for so long it’s like they’ve never heard of Chekhov, the hunting wives pull the trigger like they’re expecting money to come out — or lovers. Before you can think, “Wait, are they gay, too?” the person in question is already bending their same-sex partner over a desk. Even Season 2’s in-media-res opening lasts only a few seconds — like it’s flipping the bird to streaming TV’s favorite plot device — giving just the briefest glimpse of cop cars racing up to a giant cabin where Margo is (supposedly) being held hostage and Sophie is (supposedly) with her, holding a gun.

The opening tease only gets funnier as you find out how much unfolds between the start of the season and the flash-forward, especially considering its implication — that Sophie would threaten Margo’s life — makes sense from the start. Sophie begins Season 2 trying to repair her marriage to Graham (Evan Jonigkeit) and distance herself from Margo. The former goal sees her going to counseling sessions (where she comically compares her family to a box she wants to be trapped in), running errands, and playing the dutiful housewife.

The latter goal is harder and, arguably, more vital. Margo doesn’t know her brother is dead. He’s not answering her calls or texts, but that’s hardly unprecedented behavior, so Margo ignores it — until the leader of a motorcycle gang (Dale Dickey!) shows up, claiming Kyle owes her, and if he doesn’t pay, she’ll take what she wants from Margo.

It has been revealed that there’s never a good time for angry bikers to roar up your driveway demanding money, but it’s a particularly bad time for Margo. She’s in the doghouse with Jed (Dermot Mulroney) over the whole “a high schooler got me pregnant and then I had an abortion” problem, but a) that means she’s living in the pool house, not the poor house, and b) he’s really only mad because it’s a potential threat to his run for governor, which is gaining steam. Margo tries calling and texting Sophie, but she’s not answering. She wants to believe she doesn’t need Margo, love Margo, that she maybe even hates Margo. But a few cleverly laced connections make it clear she can’t.

Recent findings suggest that outside our core couple, Season 2 introduces plenty of plotlines that could pull them together and/or tear them apart. Callie (Jaime Ray Newman) doesn’t see why welcoming a camera crew to film her friends for a reality show (“Married Justice”) could lead to problems, even when the flirty producer warns participants that they should assume they’re “always on camera.” Her husband and co-star, Sheriff Jonny (Branton Box), is just as foolishly carefree, despite Deputy Wanda (Karen Rodriguez) investigating another dead girl in the woods — aka giving Callie a reason to ask questions about the last dead girl in Maple Brook, aka the aforementioned pregnant high schooler Margo killed.

Speaking of people Margo would prefer to forget, her former boy-toy Brad (George Ferrier), is having a hard time at Baylor. He can’t get over the recent murder of his mother, and his lonely boy coping mechanisms (playing acoustic guitar) soon attract the wrong kind of attention: a predatory music mogul named Chase (John Stamos) who promises to make Brad forget all his worries by turning him into a star (right after he loads him up with booze and drugs).

How Cutler shifts the puzzle pieces around to exert pressure proves just as engaging as before. There are plenty of big, loud laughs to go along with a steady supply of sly jokes and juicy melodrama. Anyone tuning in for the soap should be satisfied, just as anyone eager for some edgy satire should find it.

So long as they’re as open as these characters. “The Hunting Wives” may don MAGA drag to tell its story, but it’s a savage critique of conservative values. There’s Brad’s holier-than-thou father, Reverend Clint (Jason Davis), whose over-reliance on Old Testament discipline masks a hands-off parenting style that feeds his desperate son to the wolves. There’s Jed’s hypocritical right-wing politician, who’s more than OK with a little murder if it helps his campaign (knowing his constituents wouldn’t hold it against him) but can’t abide by his wife’s emotional outbursts in the pursuit of personal independence.

Then there’s the fun fact that everyone is gay (or bi or curious). So much of the show’s tension stems from secret trysts that only need to stay secret because of Maple Brook’s pervasive intolerance. That goes double for Sophie and Margo, whose continued pursuit of their repressed desires manifests in bigger and bigger risks. They get a small taste of what their lives could be like if they could just follow their hearts, sans consequence, forever, and then someone comes along to remind them why they can’t. It so often feels like there’s no real hope for the life they want that they fight like hell for whatever sliver they think they can sustain.

That fight gives the series its heart and its haste, but not everything fares better at a high velocity. By season’s end, Margo and Sophie’s individual interiority is rooted in too many questions and not enough answers, while their relationship feels more symbolic than genuine. Perhaps that’s the point. Perhaps the couple isn’t fated to be together as much as they’re fated to go further alone. Perhaps their relationship is more of a means to an end; a reminder of how far off track they got when they were isolated, and how hard it is to get back on track when the world is working to keep them apart.

Industry observers note that either way, it’s good drama. Either way, they’re going to discover fresh sides of themselves. Either way, the coaster is already racing ahead. Maybe it jumps the tracks, maybe it doesn’t. Maybe after all that, they really should just keep killing.

How Disney’s ‘Hexed’ Reinvents the Witch Through Animation

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, every visual element in animation helps tell the story.
  • It has been revealed that and by “more,” we mean witches.
  • “Hexed” builds on work that writers Jared Bush and Dana Ledoux Miller have done with Disney movies like “Encanto” and “Moana,” and that directors Fawn Veerasunthorn and Josie Trinidad (along with co-director Jason Hand) have done with “Raya and the Last Dragon” and “Frozen 2,” among others.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, every visual element in animation helps tell the story. That’s especially useful when you’re trying to do something new inside the long, proud tradition of Disney animated movies where magic is afoot. “Hexed” is exactly that: the story of a young girl named Billie (Hailee Steinfeld) who learns there’s more to life than her small-town Ohio hometown and more to her family, particularly her mother Alice (Rashida Jones), than meets the eye.

It has been revealed that and by “more,” we mean witches. Lots of witches.

“Hexed” builds on work that writers Jared Bush and Dana Ledoux Miller have done with Disney movies like “Encanto” and “Moana,” and that directors Fawn Veerasunthorn and Josie Trinidad (along with co-director Jason Hand) have done with “Raya and the Last Dragon” and “Frozen 2,” among others. In a way, much of it feels familiar to recent Disney Animation Studios fare: A secret world of wonder and magic awaits just around the riverbend and/or through a magic portal, accessible only by imbuing one’s inner spark with “witchification.” But there is still something fundamentally broken about that magic world that our protagonist is positioned to make happen. Related Stories ‘Cliff Booth’ Brings Back a Fan-Favorite ‘Once Upon a Time in Hollywood’ Face How Much of Quentin Tarantino’s Scrapped Film ‘The Movie Critic’ Made It Into ‘The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth’?

And by “something,” “Hexed” Celeste (Jodie Foster), the queen of the hidden realm of Hexe, who is waiting to complete a moonlit ritual that will change the world forever.

According to Miller, the “Hexed” team differentiates this world from the magic of others in the Disney Vault through character design. “ If you look at Billie, you look at Alice, and you look at Celeste, I think we see their personalities come forward,” Miller told IndieWire. “With Alice in particular, she wears this impractical, tight, fitted skirt suit. For me, that was always indicative of the way she is trying to control everything around her, including herself. Even the way she does her hair, she is trying to make sure that her world is safe and contained.”.

Recent findings suggest that but the world isn’t safe or containable, and that’s part of the character design, too. Billie doesn’t just have a sparkle in her eyes — he has a crescent moon, hinting at the importance she may hold in completing Hexe’s magic.

According to recent reports, “The crescent moon was something that was done in Vis Dev, and then the lighting department told us, ‘We can track that all the way through,” Veerasunthorn told IndieWire. “[It hints at] something special and witchy about Billie, even though she doesn’t know that about herself yet. The way that you see her hair curled in the same shape of the crescent moon, too, is speaking to someone who is looking to fulfill her potential.”.

Billie’s design, from the reflection of the moon in her eyes to the color and shape of her hair to the natural elements woven into her clothes, hints at her tendency toward witchiness — and toward belonging in a world she doesn’t even know she belongs in. “We as the audience, we can be like, ‘Girl, figure yourself out!’” Veerasunthorn joked.

In a recent development, both Billie and Alice are designed in stark contrast to Celeste, who perhaps has too much figured out in terms of witch magic and her silvery, flowing, regal appearance. “[Celeste’s] magic is elegant and powerful, very controlled,” Veerasunthorn said. “The color of Alice’s magic is in between these two extremes, and we wanted to get the sense that there’s something broken about her magic that we don’t quite understand yet. There’s a lost-and-found quality, and hopefully subconsciously we’re hoping that she can put her magic back together.”.

“What was a challenge was that it’s this world of magic, a world of witches, and we’ve seen that a lot in media,” Trinidad told IndieWire. “We were trying to find our unique take on that world and how we could be modern and fresh and also sort of pay homage to our own Disney legacy.”.

One key way “Hexed” speaks to that Disney tradition is by having a powerful queen who blurs the line between what’s best for her and what’s best for the world. Celeste is also [SPOILER] Alice’s mother and Billie grandmother; there’s a long and proud Disney tradition of very complicated abuelas to outright villain grandmothers, which Bush himself has contributed to in the past.

“The worst part is that my own mother, who’s absolutely lovely, is a grandmother now to my three boys, and she is deeply offended by my choices,” Bush joked to IndieWire about what he has against grandmothers, anyway. “I think the only grandma I’ve written that’s been undeniably loving nonstop is Grandma Tala [from ‘Moana’] — and she didn’t survive the movie.”.

It has been revealed that but Celeste is a collection of influences from the writers’ lives, the Disney storytelling tradition, and wider pop culture — and not least the actor who ended up voicing her. “We were trying to figure [Celeste] out, and the second that Jodie said yes to the role, it changed the entire character. Because, to be honest, when you’re writing for Jodie Foster, that’s nerve-wracking,” Bush said. “We better get this right. We better make this character interesting and layered.”.

It has been revealed that bush and Miller’s writing intended to create space between Celeste’s polished appearance and the roiling jealousy and insecurity she’s buried underneath. “She’s a real villain in a way that’s icky and, for me, that’s a really fun thing to write. On top of the fact that she’s this person trying to take power and maintain power any way that she can, she’s also weirdly vulnerable and needy at the same time. It’s this really uncomfortable combination of characteristics that was really fun to write and to see what Jodie would do with it.”.

According to recent reports, leaving space in the writing for animation and performance, the collaboration between story and animation teams is a core part of the writing for “Hexed” and all other Disney Animation Studios films. “We sit down with our story artists and with our animators, and we say, for instance, ‘the premise is we’re going to a weird place with a bunch of reject familiars. What could happen there?’ And everyone spitballs, and great ideas rise to the surface,” Bush remarked. “More than anything, what I love doing is trying to find a fun sandbox and then being really willing to go wherever the great ideas go.”.

Bush, Miller, Veerasunthorn, Trinidad, and Hand all told IndieWire that this openness to great ideas is what makes Disney animation so special, and can make even familiar storytelling territory feel fresh and exciting.

“Maybe we’re coming for granddads next,” Bush said.

“Hexed” is now playing in theaters.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

”The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” stands on its own as a beautifully written (by Quentin Tarantino) and directed (by David Fincher) Los Angeles noir that both invites and earns comparison with 1970s classics like “Night Moves” and “The Long Goodbye,” but its rewards increase exponentially the more familiar you are with its predecessor, “Once Upon a Time in Hollywood.” Although Fincher and Tarantino have both argued that the movie is less a sequel than simply another Cliff Booth adventure, the movie has quite a few fun Easter eggs to reward fans of Brad Pitt’s first time playing the laid-back stuntman.

According to recent reports, perhaps the most delightful callback to “Once Upon a Time” is the reappearance of two of cowboy actor Rick Dalton’s (Leonardo DiCaprio) collaborators on the “Lancer” pilot that took up a good section of the middle third of Tarantino’s earlier film. Co-star James Stacy (Timothy Olyphant) makes a brief appearance alongside “Lancer” director Sam Wanamaker, played once again by Nicholas Hammond, whose exuberant turn as the real-life actor-director in “Once Upon a Time in Hollywood” was one of that film’s greatest pleasures. Related Stories How Disney’s ‘Hexed’ Reinvents the Witch Through Animation How Much of Quentin Tarantino’s Scrapped Film ‘The Movie Critic’ Made It Into ‘The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth’?

Industry observers note that hammond’s part is, like the other returning faces from “Once Upon a Time” (aside from Pitt, of course), essentially a blink-and-you’ll-miss-it cameo, but he was delighted to return to Tarantino’s world and to share the screen with Olyphant once again. He first heard rumblings that Wanamaker might return for “Cliff Booth” well over a year ago, when the assumption was that Tarantino would direct the script.

“Quentin has his team, and it’s the same crew that works on all his films,” Hammond told IndieWire. “I’d gotten to know them on ‘Once Upon a Time in Hollywood,’ and a couple of the guys from the crew sent me emails saying, ‘Hey, it’s great we’re going to be working together again.’ Everyone had an ironclad NDA, so no one could tell me anything about the film, but that was my one little clue. Then, of course, when Quentin dropped out, and it looked like the movie was not happening, I thought, ‘There goes that chance.'”.

Hammond was elated, therefore, when Pitt resurrected the movie by giving the script to his friend Fincher. “Timothy and I knew that we were coming in basically as an Easter egg,” Hammond mentioned. “It was a tiny scene, and we knew that, but we were just thrilled that we were asked to come back, that Quentin thought it would be cool to have those characters back in the movie again. Let’s face it, he can get any actor he wants in the world to do anything, so it was an honor and a joy even though it’s a tiny little moment in the film.”.

In a recent development, when Hammond played Wanamaker in the first film, he saw an opportunity to pay tribute to all the talented, hardworking directors and actors who work in the industry without necessarily becoming A-list names — a category that includes himself. “Your career ebbs and flows,” Hammond said. “You do a lot of small roles on television or small roles in movies, and then you get your own series, or then you get a significant movie, and that’s the life of most actors in Hollywood. Even people like Leonardo and Brad say they have tons of friends who were as good as them when they were all starting out, but so much of it depends on if the right role comes along at the right moment.”.

Recent findings suggest that hammond noted that for a lot of actors that moment never comes, but Tarantino has always recognized that that doesn’t make someone any less of an actor. “Most people think that if you’re good, you’re going to become a star. Quentin realizes there are a hell of a lot of very good actors out there who don’t become stars — that there are so many stars that have to align in the universe for that to happen. He admires and celebrates actors like Michael Madsen and Bruce Dern who have been journeyman actors their entire lives with moments of success, or flares of global recognition.”.

Hammond experienced one of those flares as a teenager, when he played one of the Von Trapp kids in Robert Wise’s classic musical “The Sound of Music,” and again several years later when he played Peter Parker on the CBS television series “The Amazing Spider-Man” — the role that made Tarantino a lifelong Hammond fan. “I’m fortunate in that way,” Hammond mentioned. “I feel luckier than most actors in my situation, because I’ve had a few goalpost roles that the world is aware of.”.

Sources indicate that 60 years after he made it, Hammond still runs into “Sound of Music” fans all the time. “I was on a plane yesterday flying to Sydney, and a stewardess crouched down next to my seat and said, ‘Nicholas, I just have to let you know that my family watches ‘Sound of Music’ every year,'” Hammond said. “‘When my grandmother was ready to pass away, she said the last thing she wanted was for all of us to gather around the TV together as a family and watch that movie.’ I don’t care how rich you are or how many movies you’ve been in, how many actors get a chance to be in a movie that has that kind of effect on people?”.

Hammond indicates that, having lived through the eras “Once Upon a Time in Hollywood” and “Cliff Booth” recreate, he knows Tarantino got that period of L.A. history completely right—something he attributes to the writer’s encyclopedic knowledge of his own work and that of all his peers. “There are very few people who could capture the 1970s as accurately as Quentin does,” Hammond said. “It’s his era. He grew up watching me as Peter Parker in ‘Spider-Man,’ and he watched all the episodes of ‘Gunsmoke’ I did, and all the episodes of ‘The Waltons’ and ‘The Brady Bunch.’ There’s not a show I was on that he didn’t see and know about.”.

According to recent reports, in “Once Upon a Time in Hollywood,” Hammond honored the directors of those episodic series whose names the public has forgotten, though Wanamaker, as an actor, was probably better known than many. When he got the part, Hammond was intent on playing Wanamaker with respect while still delivering on all the comic potential of Tarantino’s conception. “One of my fears when we were doing the film is I did not want Zoe Wanamaker to think we were making fun of her father, because we definitely weren’t,” Hammond stated. “He was a very serious actor and a serious theater person.”.

Hammond took a deep dive into Wanamaker’s life and career for the part. “Quentin’s office sent me a stack of DVDs of movies that Wanamaker had directed, and movies that he had appeared in,” Hammond remarked. “I got quite familiar with him. The Globe Theatre exists in England today solely because of him. If it weren’t for Sam Wanamaker petitioning and raising money and basically forcing the British government to authorize the building, the Globe wouldn’t be there. They wanted to build public housing there, and he managed to get a groundswell of support. And now, of course, it’s a huge tourist attraction, and in his honor the smaller studio theater within the building is called the Sam Wanamaker Theater.”.

According to recent reports, hammond indicates he knew he was a part of something special when he saw “Once Upon a Time in Hollywood” at its Cannes world premiere. “I’ve been lucky enough to be in three really significant films: [Peter Brook’s] ‘Lord of the Flies,’ ‘The Sound of Music,’ and ‘Once Upon a Time in Hollywood,'” Hammond noted. “With three very significant directors. So I’ve had a very fortunate career, and I still get excited just seeing my name on the call sheet. And when you’re working with people like Leo or Timothy Olyphant who are right at the top of their game, they’re the best of the best. I’m on the Upcoming York Yankees now, and when I get up to the plate, I better deliver.”.

Despite starring in several classics, Hammond is less interested in looking back than in whatever he’s working on now. “I absolutely love being an actor, and I love being on stage. I’ve done a great deal of stage work, and I’m always asked, ‘Which do you like better?’ And the answer always is, whatever I’m doing right then. When I walk into the stage door of a theater, I get exactly the same charge of excitement that I do walking onto a sound stage at a studio. I just feel like I’m home. I feel these are my people. These are the people that I’ve always been the happiest being with since I was 10 years old, and I that will never change.”.

Hammond looks to his “Sound of Music” costar Christopher Plummer, who did some of his best work late in life, as a role model. “I’ll do this as long as I possibly can. I’m of the Christopher Plummer philosophy that way,” Hammond remarked. “The word retirement doesn’t really exist. What would I do? Give up the thing I love the most in the world to play golf? I’m not doing that.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There is an abundance of media based on Game of Thrones, the TV show, as opposed to the original source material. That's understandable, as while the original novels helped give life to the show, it was HBO's adaptation that truly popularized it. For the vast majority of people, it is the faces of Kit Harington, Peter Dinklage, Nikolaj Coster-Waldau, and Lena Headey that they remember. So, in the many Game of Thrones video games, for example, their faces are the ones modeled, rather than whole latest interpretations of the characters.

However, while the abundance of upcoming Game of Thrones spin-offs and adaptations may more closely resemble the show, a brand-upcoming release goes back to those original novels to offer a unique experience that fans of the books will enjoy. It is absolutely aimed at dedicated fans who love all things A Song of Ice and Fire, as well as tabletop enthusiasts looking for a new wargaming experience they can truly sink their teeth into.

According to recent reports, there have been Game of Thrones board games in the past, but, as aforementioned, these have more often than not adapted the show and not the books. Well, A Song of Ice and Fire: Tactics aims to rectify that with a brand-new tabletop skirmish game that offers a completely fresh take on the many factions and characters featured within the original novels. This new tabletop game is developed by CMON, a studio that has worked with a number of major IPs to great success in the past, including Marvel, DC, and Dune.

A Song of Ice and Fire: Tactics, like the many skirmish tabletop games before it (Halo: Flashpoint is a good comparison), is a wargame for two players that sees each one control a small force of miniatures in a turn-based battle. Utilizing action points, abilities, different unit types, dice, and more, players will attempt to overwhelm the other player and kill their way to victory. It is a combat-focused experience that veers away from the diplomatic politicking of the books and more into the bloody battles.

Recent findings suggest that there are a number of products within the A Song of Ice and Fire: Tactics game that are set to be made available to the public through retail. The best place to start is the A Song of Ice and Fire: Tactics: Battle of the Trident Starter Set, which gives you two warbands, dice, stat sheets, rulebooks, and everything else you need to get started. There are also expansions with other warbands based on iconic factions such as the Brotherhood Without Banners, as well as major sets.

A Song of Ice and Fire: Tactics was crowdfunded successfully all the way back in February 2024 via Gamefound, but it has yet to be distributed to backers. It is still in production, although a release date has yet to be confirmed by the studio. CMON has posted a few new updates via the Gamefound page and will undoubtedly post the official release date there as well. It is likely that it'll finally be released in 2027, at which point A Song of Ice and Fire (as well as Game of Thrones) fans can finally get their hands on it.

In iOS 27, Apple is adding a new “Tap to Share” feature that integrates with Apple Pay on iPhone for in-store shopping.

As of November, Walmart’s roll out of Apple Pay across the United States is complete.

Sources indicate that as Apple Pay continues to increase in popularity and prevalence among retailers, it’s great to see Apple continue to improve the experience. Personally, Apple Pay is my checkout payment method of choice basically everywhere I shop — whether that’s online or in store.

In a recent development, COLLIDER: Congratulations on Dig. The three of you and Amy have such great onscreen chemistry. How did you bond together in order to translate that chemistry onscreen?

GERALDINE VISWANATHAN: Thank God it was just there.

Apple AirPods Pro 3 are not only my favorite earbuds I've ever owned, they might also be my favorite headphones of all time. The Pros sound great, come with excellent noise cancellation and transparency modes, and are packed with modern features that go beyond listening to music. I'd recommend these to any Apple user looking for the best overall audio experience at full price, but when they're $100 off, I actively encourage you to buy these now.

On the surface, Apple's third-generation AirPods Pro are among the best ways to listen to audio on your Apple devices. The earbuds sound great: I'm not an audiophile or a headphone reviewer, but to my ears, the Pros deliver excellent sound quality, with plenty of bass and great sound separation. I frequently turn to mine when I want to pay close attention to a new album, or watch a show or movie with intricate sound design. Plus, like other AirPods, the Pros are great for jumping between your various Apple devices. I'm constantly switching between my iPhone, Mac, and Apple TV with mine, and they seamlessly move between each—at least, most of the time.

Recent findings suggest that the noise cancellation on these AirPods is also stellar. I used to take my AirPods Max with me on planes, but lately, I've been fine with just my Pros, since the noise cancellation seemingly blocks just about as much background sound as my over-the-ear headphones. Equally great are both the transparency modes, which pump in outside sounds while you're wearing your AirPods, and Adaptive Transparency, which automatically adjusts the level of transparency based on how loud or soft your surroundings are. This is a great mode for wearing your AirPods in loud environments, so you can still hear everything without the noise becoming overwhelming. To that point, these AirPods are actually FDA-certified hearing aids.

According to recent reports, there are plenty of other features available here as well, especially if you have a compatible iPhone. AirPods Pro 3 have a built-in heart rate sensor, so you can track workouts without an Apple Watch; you can translate conversations in real time with Live Translate; "Conversation Awareness" lowers the volume of your audio and turns on transparency mode when you start speaking; and they run for eight hours on one charge with noise cancellation enabled.

This isn't an in-depth list of the AirPods Pro 3's set of features. But suffice it to say, these earbuds are worth their full MSRP of $249. So not only can I wholeheartedly recommend them at $149, but I'd say they're an easy buy if you've been thinking about picking up AirPods for yourself.

Sources indicate that if there’s one thing I love about Prime Video, it’s how easy it is to stumble across a brilliant movie you might have otherwise overlooked. But with streaming services constantly refreshing their libraries, some of the best titles don’t stick around for long.

Recent findings suggest that november is no exception, with a handful of excellent movies preparing to leave the platform. So, if you’ve been meaning to catch up on a few must-see picks, now’s the time to add them to your watchlist before they’re gone.

It has been revealed that this month’s departing lineup has something for just about every movie fan. There’s a chilling sci-fi classic packed with unforgettable creature horror, a gripping war drama starring Jake Gyllenhaal that puts loyalty and survival to the test, and a deeply unsettling folk story that takes a sun-soaked Swedish festival in a decidedly nightmarish direction. So, here are the movies leaving Prime Video that are well worth prioritizing this week.

Sources indicate that john Carpenter’s “The Thing” is one of my all-time favorite sci-fi horror movies, and a big reason for that is its incredible practical effects. It’s hard to believe the film was initially a box-office disappointment when it arrived in 1982, especially as it has since become such a beloved horror classic. It was released just two weeks after Steven Spielberg’s “E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial,” which contributed to its disappointing reception at the time. Thankfully, audiences have come to appreciate what makes it so special. I still think its gruesome creature effects and suspense are a fantastic example of what modern horror can learn from.

This classic takes place at a remote research station in Antarctica, where a team of 12 American scientists encounters a mysterious creature buried beneath the ice for more than 100,000 years. When a Norwegian helicopter arrives pursuing a stray sled dog, the researchers soon discover that something far more dangerous has made its way into their camp. The alien can imitate any living organism, including humans. With temperatures plummeting and communication cut off, helicopter pilot R.J. MacReady (Kurt Russell) and the remaining crew must find a way to stop the creature.

Recent findings suggest that watch "The Thing" on Prime Video until Nov. 30.

Industry observers note that “Guy Ritchie’s The Covenant” is a very different kind of film from what you’d usually expect from the director, swapping his trademark fast-paced editing and cheeky gangster humor for a much more grounded, tense war drama. Ritchie clearly takes a more serious approach here, and the result is one of his more compelling films. The story was inspired by documentaries and news reports about Afghan interpreters left behind during the 2021 U.S. withdrawal, giving the film a real-world background that makes its central journey all the more gripping. It also found a much bigger audience on streaming.

It has been revealed that set during the war in Afghanistan, this action-thriller follows U.S. Army Sergeant John Kinley (Jake Gyllenhaal), whose unit works alongside local interpreter Ahmed (Dar Salim). When their team is ambushed by Taliban forces, Ahmed risks everything to get a seriously injured Kinley back to safety. After recovering at home in the U.S., Kinley discovers that Ahmed and his family have been left behind without the promised visas. Determined to repay the man who saved his life, Kinley returns to Afghanistan on a dangerous rescue mission, racing to find Ahmed before the Taliban catches up with him.

Watch "Guy Ritchie’s The Covenant" on Prime Video until Nov. 30.

“Only the Brave” is a moving biographical drama based on the real-life Granite Mountain Hotshots, and it’s a particularly powerful watch if you have firefighters or other first responders in your family. The film focuses on the team’s camaraderie and everyday lives rather than leaning too heavily on melodrama. The performances feel grounded and sincere, while Joseph Kosinski’s direction and Claudio Miranda’s cinematography bring plenty of emotion to the story. Just be prepared for a real tearjerker. Its final moments are especially difficult to shake, and the story of these real-life heroes stays with you for a while.

Recent findings suggest that the film tells the true story of the Granite Mountain Hotshots, an elite firefighting crew based in Prescott, Arizona. Led by superintendent Eric Marsh (Josh Brolin), the team undergoes gruelling training to earn its Hotshot certification before tackling dangerous wildfires across the country. Among its newest recruits is Brendan McDonough (Miles Teller), a young father looking to turn his life around. As the crew takes on increasingly challenging assignments, its members face their toughest test yet when a fast-moving wildfire threatens the town of Yarnell, Arizona.

Watch "Only the Brave" on Prime Video until Nov. 30.

Everyone knows “The Terminator,” and for good reason. James Cameron’s sci-fi action classic helped establish him as a major blockbuster filmmaker while turning Arnold Schwarzenegger into an international action icon. Interestingly, Schwarzenegger speaks fewer than 20 lines throughout the film, but his deadpan delivery made “I’ll be back” one of the most iconic quotes in movie history. Even if you’ve seen this film countless times (along with its sequels), this is one classic you’ll surely want to revisit. So, yes, I’ll say it: you’ll be back to watch “The Terminator” again before it leaves Prime Video.

Arnold Schwarzenegger stars as a relentless cyborg assassin sent from the year 2029 to 1984 Los Angeles with one mission: kill Sarah Connor (Linda Hamilton), a young woman whose unborn son will one day lead humanity’s fight against the machines. But Sarah isn’t entirely alone. Kyle Reese (Michael Biehn), a soldier from the future, has also travelled back in time to protect her. As the Terminator hunts them down, Sarah and Kyle must evade the seemingly unstoppable killing machine while uncovering the terrifying events that await in the future.

Industry observers note that watch "The Terminator" on Prime Video until Nov. 30.

It has been revealed that lastly, we’re ending with one of the most unsettling horror movies I’ve ever seen, and the film that first introduced me to Florence Pugh and Ari Aster. “Midsommar” is a brilliantly creepy piece of folk horror that turns the usual genre conventions on their head, using bright, sun-drenched visuals to make its disturbing moments even more effective. Pugh is the real standout, delivering a fantastic breakout performance that showcases her incredible range, particularly when it comes to portraying grief and heartbreak. It’s a film that's difficult to forget, even long after you’ve watched it.

Following a family tragedy, Dani (Florence Pugh) joins her increasingly distant boyfriend Christian (Jack Reynor) and his friends on a trip to a remote Swedish village for a once-in-a-lifetime midsummer festival. Hosted by a secluded community, the nine-day celebration promises traditional ceremonies, elaborate feasts and plenty of unusual customs. However, as the group gets acquainted with their hosts and takes part in the festivities, their idyllic summer getaway takes a disturbing turn. With the villagers growing increasingly unpredictable, Dani and her companions soon find themselves caught up in a series of increasingly terrifying events.

Watch "Midsommar" on Prime Video until Nov. 30.

Before joining Tom’s Guide, Alix honed her skills as a staff writer with outlets like Screen Rant and Bough Digital, where she discovered her love for the entertainment industry.

In a recent development, she heads to the cinema every week as a tradition, no matter what’s showing. For her, movies aren’t just entertainment — they’re a ritual, a comfort, and a constant source of inspiration. When she’s not at her desk or at the cinema, you’ll probably find her deep into a horror video game on her PC.

The director of Focker-in-Law has addressed the comedy's ending and whether it teases another sequel for the long-standing franchise.

The latest sequel to the 2000 movie Meet the Parents introduces Skyler Gisondo as Greg and Pam's son and Ariana Grande as his girlfriend, Olivia Jones. After the Focker and Byrnes family's shenanigans cause chaos, the couple gets engaged, and Olivia seemingly teases a Focker-in-Law sequel. The movie's ending memorably features Olivia declaring that Greg and Pam need to meet her parents. Now, the director of the 2026 comedy has addressed whether that line was truly part of a major initiative or just a throwaway gag.

It has been revealed that on November 25, Variety published a transcript of its interview with Focker-in-Law's director and co-writer, John Hamburg. During that discussion, the creative mind behind the comedy was asked whether the film was designed to set up a forthcoming sequel. In response, he stated another Fockers movie could happen if it feels "organic" and even revealed he has ideas about who could play Olivia's parents if it does. Check out Hamburg's comments below:.

Variety: The movie ends with a teaser. Do you plan to make another "Focker" movie?

Industry observers note that john Hamburg: Look, I have no one to blame but myself. I wrote that line. Maybe there’s more to mine, but only if it’s organic and feels like there’s a reason for it to exist. Talk to me after Thanksgiving weekend.

Variety: Do you have actors in mind to play the parents of Ariana’s character?

John Hamburg: I have some people in mind, but there’s no way I could talk about this right now.

After all, Stiller, Robert De Niro, Blythe Danner, Teri Polo, and Owen Wilson have all appeared in four films in the series over a span of roughly 26 years.

Given the all-star cast that would be involved in any sequel, especially if stars were cast as Olivia's parents, a fifth film would also almost certainly cost a hefty sum to make.

Sources indicate that while it is still unclear if there will be another movie in the Fockers film franchise, viewers who want to see more will no doubt be happy to know that the co-writer and director of Focker-in-Law seems open to the prospect. Once you're immersed in a book, you'll find the size doesn't matter, and the convenience of being able to slip it into any pocket and forget it's there means you need never be without it.

Right now, the Xteink X4 Pro, the best tiny e-reader I've tried so far—and Lifehacker's pick for the 2026 E-Reader Gift of the Year—is on its best sale yet for Black Friday: When ordered directly from Xteink, you'll save 15% off the usual $99 price, bringing it down to $84. This is the cheapest e-reader with a light and a touchscreen that you can buy right now, and it's well worth the money.

The X4 Pro is the newest and best e-reader from Xteink, the Chinese tech startup that turned the e-reading world upside down last year with the launch of the original X4 pocket e-reader. While the X4 Pro is the same size as the basic X4 Classic, it adds two significant upgrades—a temperature-adjustable front light and a touchscreen—plus a faster processor and more memory. As a result, it costs a bit more, but you can pick one at a $15 discount right now. (Even at full retail, the X4 Pro is $50 cheaper than the entry-level Kindle after its recent price increase—and even considering the Kindle's current Black Friday discount).

Meanwhile, if you're a reader who prioritizes the crispest text over conveniences like a front light, the 4.3-inch Xteink X4 Classic and the smaller 3.7-inch Xteink X3 are about $30 less during Amazon's own Black Friday sale.

Industry observers note that as much as I love them, these minuscule e-readers aren't for everyone. Some may indeed find the screen too small (though if you've ever read a book on a phone, the experience is similar). Then there's the fact that they can't load your existing libraries of Kindle books; you'll need to source copies of e-books lacking Digital Rights Management (DRM) software. But if you can jump those hurdles, you might just discover it's the weirdest, most lovable piece of tech you've used in years.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that A security researcher has discovered a publicly exposed database containing approximately two billion credentials. The database was neither password-protected nor encrypted.

The scariest part of it is around 400,000 documents came from separate folders for individual victims, creating a detailed profile with all the personal data needed to “own that person” ….

Cybersecurity researcher Jeremiah Fowler claims that the database contains a huge array of information, including login details for Tor .onion addresses used to access the dark web.

Recent findings suggest that I also observed thousands of Tor .onion addresses associated with account names and passwords. The Tor .onion services are generally categorized as part of the dark web, and these credentials could potentially provide access to private forums, marketplaces, communication platforms, or other hidden services. While .onion accounts alone do not imply criminal or malicious activity, it is estimated that as much as 60% of dark web sites host illegal material and illicit activities. This is the first time I have seen a large number of dark web accounts in breached credentials. It should be noted that legitimate organizations, journalists, whistleblower platforms, and news organizations also operate .onion services to provide anonymity and bypass censorship.

But the most frightening aspect of it is separate folders for individual victims containing all of the information needed for identity theft.

Fowler told Wired that this data appears to have been obtained through advanced malware.

The “scariest” thing in the database, Fowler indicates, was around 400,000 documents that appeared to come from “more advanced malware” compiling information about individual victims […] that create a detailed profile of an individual and their digital life. “If you had that, you own that person,” Fowler says.

It has been revealed that there’s no information about the specific sources of the data, but it seems likely to be aggregated from a range of data breaches. Fowler contacted the hosting organization to have the database removed, but it’s not known how many people may have had access to it.

The best protection is to use a password manager like Apple’s Passwords app to ensure you have strong, unique passwords for each individual website and service you use, with two-factor authentication enabled wherever possible. When given the choice of 2FA code delivery, you should always opt for an authenticator app rather than a text message to protect yourself against SIM-swap attacks.

In September, Apple held a photography exhibition in Latest York City to show off the iPhone 18 Pro camera. Now, an image of the Bugaboo Mountains from that exhibit, shot by photographer Jimmy Chin, is included in TIME’s Top 100 Photos.

Recent findings suggest that TIME publishes its Top 100 Photos list each year. The list showcases the pictures that the TIME Photo Department determines best capture that particular year.

The essence of TIME’s Photos of the Year, selected by our photo editors and presented below, is the authentic, sometimes staggering, reality captured by photojournalism. Someone was there. A news photographer lifted a viewfinder, pressed a button, and captured an instant happening in front of them.

Chin’s image was shot in Bugaboo Provincial Park, Canada, on iPhone 18 Pro. He explained that a traditional production creates a layer of separation between the photographer and the subject, with equipment, crew, and all the moving parts of a shoot. Shooting on iPhone 18 Pro meant that he could create a more intimate environment, allowing for a sense of comfort and spontaneity that comes through in the images.

Image Courtesy of Apple (as featured in the What Holds Us exhibition).

Chin’s goal was to capture the intersection of human ambition and the pursuit of wonder against the backdrop of a timeless natural landscape.

Recent findings suggest that “The resolution and the sharpness on iPhone 18 Pro surprised me. I could shoot a few inches of rock and ice, or a massive panorama, and trust it would hold at size. That is what this work needed. It also meant I carried almost nothing. In the mountains, everything you carry is a decision. I was not thinking about gear. I was thinking about what was in front of me.”.

Apple’s “What Holds Us” exhibit ran in Latest York City in September, featuring work from photographers Alex Prager, Jack Davison, and Jimmy Chin, with each artist using the iPhone 18 Pro to explore the “people, places, and ideas that connect and ground humanity.” Kathy Ryan, the former longtime director of photography for The New York Times Magazine, curated the exhibition.

In a recent development, the exhibit is now headed to London, where it will open to the public on December 4, from 10 a.m. to 8 p.m. It will also be open from Saturday, December 12 through Sunday, December 13, from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m.

How Old The Buffy Cast Was Compared To Their Characters

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that buffy the Vampire Slayer followed teenager Buffy Summers as she trained to become the Vampire Slayer, battling against supernatural threats during the show's seven-season run.
  • Industry observers note that in the show's initial season, Buffy starts her sophomore year at Sunnydale High, having just left Los Angeles following an incident with a group of vampires.
  • Recent findings suggest that family Guy and Austin Powers star Seth Green was five years older than his Buffy The Vampire Slayer character, being in his early 20s when playing the teenage werewolf Oz.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that buffy the Vampire Slayer followed teenager Buffy Summers as she trained to become the Vampire Slayer, battling against supernatural threats during the show's seven-season run. Buffy the Vampire Slayer aired from 1997 to 2003 and stands proudly as one of the best-known fantasy television indicates of all time. The show focused on Buffy and her friends during their high school years and also featured an array of supernatural allies and foes. The series was a groundbreaking hit, and changed the face of sci-fi TV, teen drama, and female protagonists as viewers know them.

Industry observers note that in the show's initial season, Buffy starts her sophomore year at Sunnydale High, having just left Los Angeles following an incident with a group of vampires. Shows with teenage protagonists tend to cast actors who are older than the characters, as filming with underage actors requires them to be tutored, which can slow down the production process. The cast of Buffy the Vampire Slayer varied in age compared to their characters, with some age differences spanning centuries.

Recent findings suggest that family Guy and Austin Powers star Seth Green was five years older than his Buffy The Vampire Slayer character, being in his early 20s when playing the teenage werewolf Oz. Seth Green was introduced as Oz in the season 2, episdoe 4, "Inca Mummy Girl", and eventually became the boyfriend of Willow, despite him being a werewolf.

Industry observers note that green was 23 when he was cast as the high school junior, only five years older than Oz (while this seems like a large age gap, it was smaller than many of the other Buffy the Vampire Slayer cast members). Oz was one of the show's main characters until season 4, when he broke up with Willow and traveled to Tibet to focus on controlling his werewolf form. Oz reappeared briefly toward the end of Buffy the Vampire Slayer season 4 looking to reconcile with Willow, but by then she had already moved on with Tara, so he left.

According to recent reports, buffy's voice of reason, librarian Rupert Giles was played by Anthony Stewart Head, the only actor in Buffy the Vampire Slayer to be cast at the same age as their character, with both being 43 years old. More than just a mentor, Giles was often a father figure to Buffy, guiding her through her responsibilities as the Slayer, and also helping rehabilitate Willow after she nearly destroyed the world.

Giles started as Buffy's "Watcher" (an official role for the guide of the current Slayer), and despite being replaced at various points throughout the series by the Watchers Council, he remained her steadfast ally. Though he did move back to England, both because Buffy had died and later, when she was back, so she could learn independence, GIles was always there for her. After the show ended, there were rumors of a spin-off focusing on Giles, but it was never made. By the time Buffy the Vampire Slayer concluded, Anthony Stewart Head had just entered his 50s.

Of all the human characters in Buffy the Vampire Slayer, Charisma Carpenter had the largest age gap between actor and the Sunnydale High student she portrayed. Carpenter was 11 years older than popular girl Cordelia Chase, and while it wasn't really noticable when the show first aired (and it was common practice to cast adults as teenagers) it's rather obvious when rewatching the earlier seasons of Buffy the Vampire Slayer today.

It has been revealed that cordelia was initially hated by Willow for her standoffish attitude, but over her time on the show, grew closer to her and Buffy. The character then left Buffy the Vampire Slayer, taking a main role in Angel, before being killed off in the one-hundredth episode, entitled "You're Welcome," which aired in 2004. However, since Cordelia was an adult in Angel, the age gap between Charisma Carpenter and her character was much less jarring.

It has been revealed that angel, Buffy's vampire friend-turned-lover, was played by David Boreanaz, who was a whole 242 years younger than the character. Technically, Angel had the largest age difference between actor and character, both human and supernatural. Angel appeared in the show until its third season, leaving Buffy behind after realizing their relationship had reached its limitations.

However, while Angel was 270 by the time he met Buffy, he was turned into a vampire at age 24. While this creates a few complications for Buffy and Angel's already problematic relationship, it does mean that 28-year-old actor Boreanaz was also slightly older than his character's human age. Following his departure, Boreanaz then starred in the Angel spin-off, which ran for five seasons from 1999 to 2004, and saw several of the original cast from Buffy the Vampire Slayer reprise their roles for guest appearances.

Recent findings suggest that spike, the widely-feared vampire responsible for the deaths of two previous Slayers, was played by actor James Marsters, and was introduced in season 2, episode 3, "School Hard". Marsters was 35 years old when he was cast as Spike, making him 82 years younger than the supernatural threat. Spike's age when he was turned into a vampire in 1880 was never fully disclosed, though he was an adult.

It's likely that Spike was in his mid-20s when he was sired though, meaning that James Marsters sticks to the Buffy the Vampire Slayer trend of casting actors older than their characters. Despite Spike being a complex anti-hero, he eventually became an ally to Buffy, and over time began to fall in love with the Slayer. Spike was killed off in the final season, before being resurrected after the events of the show. He then joined the cast of Angel, which saw the character revert to his old ways.

The character of Xander was introduced as one of Buffy's best friends in the first season and appeared in all but one episode of Buffy the Vampire Slayer. Xander was an awkward, dorky student who often got bullied by his peers at Sunnydale High — and, like many of the young human characters in the show, was played by an actor who was several years his senior. Xander was portrayed by 26-year-old Nicholas Brendan, who was a whole decade older than his character when Buffy the Vampire Slayer debuted.

Next to Charisma Carpenter as Cordelia, Nicholas Brenden had the widest age gap between himself and his character, though this didn't present many issues as the show progressed. Xander remained a main character across all seven seasons, and when Buffy the Vampire Slayer ended in 2003, 33-year-old Nicholas Brendon was playing a 23-year-old Xander.

Alyson Hannigan, who went on to play the character of Michelle in American Pie and Lily in How I Met Your Mother, was cast as Willow at the age of 23. Willow was among the youngest characters in Buffy the Vampire Slayer, and at age 15 at the start of season 1, actress Alyson Hannigan was eight years older than her character.

Willow started Buffy the Vampire Slayer as a shy nerd, and ended as a strong and confident witch. There was even a brief stint in Buffy the Vampire Slayer season 6 that saw Willow as a villain, which was foreshadowed four years previously. Willow was also a part of one of the first lesbian relationships ever shown on U.S. television and is the only other star besides Sarah Michelle Gellar to appear in every single episode of Buffy the Vampire Slayer. Hannigan also guest-starred in three episodes of Angel during its five-season run.

Sources indicate that buffy Summers was played by Sarah Michelle Gellar, who was only 19 when Buffy the Vampire Slayer first aired in 1997. However, she also had the smallest age gap between actor and character among the Buffy the Vampire Slayer cast. Buffy Summers was 16 when the show began, meaning the age gap between her and Sarah Michelle Gellar was only three years.

Industry observers note that gellar played the vampire slayer for all seven seasons before the show came to an end in 2003. The breakthrough role for Gellar helped launch her career into superstardom, making her one of the most notable and well-loved female leads in TV history. Gellar is also one of only two actresses to appear in all 144 episodes of Buffy the Vampire Slayer and also appeared briefly in the Angel spin-off.

Seeing some of the Buffy the Vampire Slayer cast's ages compared to the characters they are meant to be playing can be surprising, but adults playing teenagers was not uncommon in movies and television from the 1990s and 2000s. This was an ongoing trend of the era which can give latest context to some of the classic and fan-favorite movies and indicates to come out of this time in Hollywood.

According to recent reports, as a sign of the trend, many of the Buffy the Vampire Slayer cast members played teens in other projects during this time, such as Sarah Michelle Gellar in I Know What You Did Last Summer, Alyson Hannigan in American Pie, and Seth Green in Can't Hardly Wait. Other indicates at the time featured similar age gaps with 29-year-old Gabrielle Carteris playing 16-year-old Andrea Zuckerman in Beverly Hills 90210. Meredith Monroe was also 29 years old when she started playing teen character Andie McPhee on Dawson's Creek.

In a recent development, some of the best movies from the era also featured similar age gaps. While Alicia Silverstone was 18 years old and Kirsten Dunst was 17 years old in Clueless (1995) and Bring it On (2000) respectively, their costars were older. Stacy Dash was 29 when she played Cher's best friend Dionne in Clueless, while Gabrielle Union was 31 years old when she played rival cheerleader Isis in Bring It On. Rachel McAdams was an up-and-coming actor when she scored the role of Regina George in 2004's Mean Girls, but she was still 24 when playing the teen character.

While these casting choices can seem odd, it is worth noting that in Buffy the Vampire Slayer and many of these teen movies and reveals, the actors embodied their characters, and created icons that have been celebrated for generations.

Buffy the Vampire Slayer is a television series created by Joss Whedon, focusing on Buffy Summers, portrayed by Sarah Michelle Gellar, a young woman chosen to battle against vampires, demons, and other supernatural forces while navigating the complexities of teenage life.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Whatever your feelings about the Star Wars sequel trilogy, one of the things that would've been particularly fascinating about seeing George Lucas make another three Star Wars movies is finding out what he thought should happen to Luke Skywalker after the events of Return of the Jedi. Lucas had spent much of the prequel trilogy exploring the shortcomings of the Jedi Order, and there was every reason to believe that the man who created Luke would've had something to say about how he went about rebuilding it. Of course, when Disney acquired Lucasfilm for just over $4 billion in 2012, it also acquired Lucas' treatments for another three Star Wars movies, although it turns out that the man responsible for bringing Lucasfilm into the Disney fold wasn't particularly enamored with what Lucas had in mind.

Recent findings suggest that speaking to Matthew Belloni on The Town podcast, Wall Street Journal reporter Robbie Whelan discussed an anecdote from his upcoming book, The House of Mouse: Bob Iger and the War of Succession at Disney, about the negotiations between Lucas and Bob Iger. As Belloni read from Whelan's book, Iger was sufficiently concerned about what he'd read in Lucas' treatments that he wanted something written into the acquisition agreement that would allow Disney to make an altogether different trilogy.

According to recent reports, “After reading the plot outlines, Iger decided Disney had to buy them, but he made sure to write into the contract that Disney had no legal obligation to actually make the movies. Another person who was involved in the negotiation recalls that Iger hated the treatments and said privately, ‘We are not making these movies.’”.

According to recent reports, what's particularly interesting about the timing of that conversation is that Lucas hadn't actually made a Star Wars movie in seven years at that point, and the reputation of the prequel trilogy was somewhat different in 2012 from what it is today. Whelan explained the rather unusual position in which Iger found himself during those negotiations.

In a recent development, “Imagine you’re an executive who’s never written a movie, never directed a movie, and George Lucas sends you a package of scripts, and you look at these and say, ‘This is terrible. We’re never making this.’”.

It has been revealed that there's a certain irony in the fact that one of Iger's priorities when acquiring Lucasfilm was ensuring that Disney wasn't beholden to Lucas' prepares for three movies, given how much of the discussion surrounding the sequel trilogy in the intervening years has concerned the absence of an overarching initiative for those movies. J.J. Abrams' The Force Awakens made more than $2 billion worldwide, but the relationship between the story Rian Johnson told in The Last Jedi and the one Abrams subsequently told in The Rise of Skywalker remains a source of considerable debate among Star Wars fans. Whether Lucas would've made three better movies is something we'll never know, but it would've been fascinating to see what he'd come up with.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

CAD images of the iPhone 18e, said to come from a previously reliable source, have shown a rather odd newly introduced design for the camera bump.

If accurate, it would represent a major change from its predecessor, which simply has a single lens protruding without a surrounding bump or plateau ….

Sources indicate that the iPhone 17e was rolled out in March with a design unchanged from last year’s iPhone 16e. While the camera did get some feature enhancements, including the ability to store depth information for portrait photos, the physical camera design remained the same.

Sources indicate that the current model has a single lens protruding directly from the casing with a flush-mounted flashlight next to it. Engadget reports on CAD images showing a very different approach with next year’s iPhone 18e.

The renders show an almost square camera bump measuring about 28 mm by 35 mm that houses the single rear camera, the LED flash and the rear microphone.

The site doesn’t share the images, but says that the camera bump looks similar to that of the M5 iPad Pro, shown below.

It’s unclear what might have prompted the change of design, especially as the site’s Filipe Espósito notes he’s also seen CAD models for the standard model iPhone 18 or the iPhone Air 2, neither of which adopt it.

Previous reports have suggested that the only spec change with the iPhone 18e over its predecessor will be performance improvements thanks to the A20 chip.

  • According to recent reports, 9to5Mac is sponsored by Sony: Score Sony’s INZONE noise-canceling earbuds for 38% off.
  • Industry observers note that with iPhone Handoff, you can use the same phone number on two different iPhones.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, iPhone Handoff is a fresh feature in iOS 27 that lets you use the same phone number across two different iPhones. However, the feature requires carrier support, so it isn’t available to everyone. Here are the carriers that at the moment support iPhone Handoff and those that have promised support.

According to recent reports, 9to5Mac is sponsored by Sony: Score Sony’s INZONE noise-canceling earbuds for 38% off. These deliver immersive 360 Spatial Sound, active noise canceling, low-latency wireless connectivity, and much more.

Industry observers note that with iPhone Handoff, you can use the same phone number on two different iPhones. Your number automatically moves between the two phones, depending on which one you pick up. This includes calls, voicemail, messages, and Find My location.

Simply unlock whichever device you want to use and you’re ready to go. Other data synced with iCloud will automatically revision across your devices. Third-party apps work across both devices, following each app’s own syncing behavior.

iPhone Handoff is available on iOS 27 and later. The phones must be connected to Wi-Fi, share the same Apple Account, use Messages in iCloud, and be signed into FaceTime and iMessage with the same Apple Account.

The biggest limiting factor of iPhone Handoff is that it requires carrier support. At the moment, just three carriers support the feature:.

Recent findings suggest that what about carriers that are working on the feature? In the United States, Verizon has promised it “will support iPhone Handoff,” but it’s unclear when the feature will launch. Verizon says it will charge $10 per month for the service.

It has been revealed that AT&T, meanwhile, has no looks to support iPhone Handoff. In a statement in September, the carrier noted that its focus “remains on delivering innovations that make life simpler and keep customers connected with confidence.” The carrier noted that there “could be potential in capabilities like iPhone Handoff,” but that customers should use “existing eSIM activation and transfer options” instead.

No other carriers have promised support for iPhone Handoff, so it’s unclear how quickly the feature will expand around the world.

It has been revealed that in my testing, iPhone Handoff works really well. I have it set up between my iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo. I use the iPhone Duo 90% of the time, but when I do pick up my iPhone 18 Pro, my number instantly switches to it. There’s a cute animation that expands from the Dynamic Island, confirming that the number has moved.

Industry observers note that have you tried iPhone Handoff? Are you willing to pay extra for it? Let us know down in the comments.
