📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that apple has three main Apple Watch "lines." There's the flagship, currently the Series 12, which represents Apple's mainstream wearable. For athletes and users who think they'll put their watches through some extreme scenarios, there's the Ultra line, currently the Apple Watch Ultra 4. And while both the Series 12 and Ultra 4 are excellent devices in their own right, they can be pretty pricey (particularly the Ultra). That's why the third category, the SE, is actually best for most people, and Lifehacker's choice for best smartwatch gift of the year. Better yet, the third-generation SE is currently $50 off ahead of Black Friday, perfect for most people asking for an Apple Watch this year.

The SE 3 does just about everything you'd expect an Apple Watch to do. It, of course, has a heart rate sensor to keep tabs on your pulse, including high and low heart rate alerts; the ability to track dozens of different workouts and exercise types (including swimming, thanks to the device's water resistance); a sleep tracker with daily analyses available in the Health app; notification forwarding to check in on your alerts without opening your iPhone; and the ability to send and receive text messages.

It comes in two sizes (40mm and 44mm) depending on how large or small you prefer your watch. No matter which model you get, the watch comes with the S10 chip, Apple's last-generation watch processor. While it isn't as fast as the current S11 chip, the S10 is more than capable of running watchOS 27. Apple says the SE 3 can run for up to 18 hours on a single charge, and up to 32 hours in Low Power Mode, with fast charging from 0% to 80% in 45 minutes.

It has been revealed that the majority of the features missing from the SE 3 aren't essential. Apple's other watches have things like bigger, brighter displays, additional health tracking tools like hypertension alerts and an ECG sensor, longer battery life, and Audio Intelligence—the latter of which might be a benefit to miss, depending on who you are.

If your giftee wants or needs any of those additional features, Series 12 or Ultra 4 might be a better choice. But for anyone who wants the essential Apple Watch experience, the SE 3 is simply the best-value watch Apple sells right now—especially at this discount. Right now, the watch starts at $199 for the 40mm watch, or $229 for the 44mm. You can also save on the cellular versions of these watches: $249 for the cellular 40mm watch, and $279 for the cellular 44mm model.

Yes, Apple participates in Black Friday, though you may want to compare their sales with other retailers like Best Buy and Walmart. So far, the best Black Friday sale on an Apple product is the M5 MacBook Air on sale for $200 off, the lowest price since the price hike this summer.

Sources indicate that black Friday sales officially begin Friday, Nov. 27, 2026, and run throughout “Cyber Week,” the five-day period that runs from Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday, Nov. 30, 2026. But Black Friday and Cyber Monday dates have expanded as retailers compete for customers. You can get the same Black Friday sales early, and we expect sales to wind down by Dec. 2, 2026.

The debate over the wisdom and safety of using Meta’s Muse AI agent continues as the app rolls out in the UK. It follows a warning by a number of regulatory bodies about the potential risks of AI agents ….

Meta yesterday announced the UK availability of Muse.

Recent findings suggest that muse, Meta’s personal Al agent, is now available to adults in the UK. Think of it as a helping hand for the jobs that pile up, like chasing a refund, renewing car insurance or keeping on top of the school calendar. To get those jobs done you can connect Muse to the apps you already use, from your email and calendar to the retailer apps you shop on.

A forum representing four different UK regulatory bodies last month issued a warning about the potential dangers involved in using AI agents. The Digital Regulation Cooperation Forum said:.

Recent findings suggest that AI agents may amplify and accelerate risks and introduce new ones. These risks may increase as the capabilities of personal agents grow and adoption rises. Questions of consumer protection, competition and data protection – for example the risk of fraud and scams, personal information sharing not in line with user expectations and misleading recommendations, decisions or information provided – must be addressed to ensure innovation develops in ways that earn and maintain public trust.

Meta has pushed back against suggestions that Muse has accessed personal data without permission, insisting that people are in control and must approve vital actions. The company has admitted to some “isolated incidents,” but says other reported breaches were either hallucinations or took place on internal versions of the app while undergoing testing. In a newly introduced blog post, Meta says:.

Muse only works with the apps and services you choose to connect it to, and you control the access it gets […] Once you’ve decided what Muse is connected to and what you want it to do, with your oversight, it can handle tasks like searching, comparing and planning for you. But before it does anything like sending an email or buying something, it shows you exactly what it’s about to do and waits for your go-ahead. A separate security agent checks Muse’s actions and the information it sends out against the permissions you’ve granted. You can also choose how often it checks in with you in Settings.

In a recent development, at the time of writing, Muse remains the second most popular free app in Apple’s US App Store, with more than 10 million downloads. We reported yesterday that some banks are already blocking AI agents, while others are warning that they will not be responsible for the consequences of any actions taken by them.

It has been revealed that time is quickly running out to watch The Accountant 2 on streaming, as the R-rated action thriller starring Jon Bernthal and Ben Affleck is leaving a major service in a couple of days. The Accountant 2 originally came out in theaters in April 2025 courtesy of Amazon MGM and director Gavin O'Connor.

In a recent development, nine years after the original thriller became a major hit, The Accountant 2 struggled to find as big an audience on the big screen. But it's since become a consistently strong performer on streaming services, starting on Prime Video before moving to other platforms. The Accountant 2 is rated R for strong violence and language throughout and has a 2-hour and 12-minute runtime.

If you're looking for a great action thriller, act fast before The Accountant 2 leaves streaming.

The Accountant 2 changed the formula of the first movie by becoming a buddy movie between Affleck and Bernthal. They reprised their roles from the first film as Christian Wolff, an autistic accountant and former assassin, and Braxton, his brother and active hitman. After only sharing a few scenes in The Accountant, the sequel leans all in on their chemistry.

Recent findings suggest that affleck and Bernthal have plenty of experience excelling in action thrillers, and they prove to be a terrific duo here. Bernthal gets to be a bit more flamboyant and charismatic, while Affleck plays things a bit more seriously. Together, they make The Accountant 2's buddy-style narrative really shine, bringing the film's action, drama, and humor to life really well.

Sources indicate that thanks to this approach, The Accountant 2 is a superior movie to the original. The first film had a solid relationship at its core between Affleck's character and Anna Kendrick's Dana Cummings, but its semi-romantic nature is absent from the sequel, allowing a brotherly bond to take center stage and go even bigger on the action.

With Bernthal's elevated role, The Accountant 2 goes farther in its R-rating. That's the plus of having two trained killers at the heart of the story rather than just one. But The Accountant 2 works so well because it finds smaller moments to have fun, like Affleck dancing in a bar, and mixes in more comedy.

Recent findings suggest that the plot can be a bit more ridiculous at times, especially with certain elements of The Accountant 2's ending, but there is a lot to like and enjoy overall. The sequel wound up scoring a 74% on Rotten Tomatoes with critics, but audiences adored the action-packed thriller, resulting in a 92% score. The Accountant has 53% and 77%, respectively.

Industry observers note that christian and Braxton's adventures aren't supposed to end with The Accountant 2, either. O'Connor confirmed years ago that he envisioned this story as a proper trilogy. He, Affleck, and screenwriter Bill Dubuque have teased The Accountant 3 being in development, but Amazon MGM has yet to give it an official green light.

Recent findings suggest that if The Accountant 3 does happen, it will bring Affleck and Bernthal back for another mission. O'Connor previously confirmed the threequel's intent to include Kendrick's return, too. Broader plot details have yet to be revealed, but the director described it as a road-trip movie bringing all three characters together.

Recent findings suggest that while The Accountant 2 will leave Hulu on December 1, it should come to another streaming service eventually. It isn't listed among Prime Video's December 2026 movies, though, so when and where it will pop back up is unclear. Go watch it now while you still can.

iOS 27 breaks 15 years of muscle memory on iPhone and iPad

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Since iOS 5 in 2011, the iPhone and iPad have included Notification Center, a central place to find alerts from various apps in chronological order.
  • Starting with iOS 27, Apple is making a major change to how users open Notification Center on iPhone and iPad.
  • Industry observers note that iOS 27 is here after a summer of beta releases.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Since iOS 5 in 2011, the iPhone and iPad have included Notification Center, a central place to find alerts from various apps in chronological order.

Starting with iOS 27, Apple is making a major change to how users open Notification Center on iPhone and iPad.

Industry observers note that iOS 27 is here after a summer of beta releases. The behavior changed slightly between the first two releases. However, this change shipped, and I’m still adjusting to it.

Opening Notification Center is unchanged on iOS 27 and iPadOS 27 by default. However, enabling Siri AI changes a key swipe gesture on both iPhone and iPad.

One of the many ways of invoking Siri AI, once enabled, is by swiping down from the center of the top edge of your iPhone or iPad display. This previously opened Notification Center.

Sources indicate that you can still access Notification Center by swiping down from the top-left corner once Siri AI is enabled. Alerts now animate in from the top left corner. This is a way to point people toward Notification Center’s smaller surface area.

According to recent reports, apple is greatly prioritizing Siri AI access in iOS 27. The majority of the top edge is devoted to invoking the new Siri experience.

The last time Apple made a change to accessing Notification Center came when Control Center moved from a swipe up gesture from the bottom to a top-right corner swipe down gesture on iPhone X. Apple later unified this experience across devices.

Now it’s Notification Center’s turn to be put in the corner. On iPadOS 27 beta 1 in particular, the area above Home screen app icons was pretty much devoted to invoking Siri AI. The area for opening Notification Center actually shrank if you disable displaying AM/PM or the date.

Industry observers note that I've been always swiping from the left corner to see my notifications. I didn't even know you could swipe from the center to get to it as well 😂 I guess I'm good then?

Apple improved this with iPadOS 27 beta 2, creating a more uniform region on either side. It’s roughly the size of two app columns with Notification Center on the left and Control Center on the right. The rest is for invoking Siri.

After 15 years of muscle memory, it’ll take some time to determine if this change is worth it or something that should be reconsidered. In the meantime, early feedback sounds overwhelmingly positive around Apple’s new Siri AI system. Hearing that Siri is good now will also take some getting used to, I’m sure.

Recent findings suggest that after months of using the new behavior, I’m certain I’d toggle it off if there were a setting to do so. Since there’s no option to disable invoking Siri from the top middle swipe down, the only thing to do is build new muscle memory around avoiding the center.

According to recent reports, what do you think? Would you change this back if you could? Is accessing Siri from the swipe-down gesture worth the change? Share your thoughts in the comments.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

One of the more effective scenes in Matt Reeves' The Batman involved Robert Pattinson's Bruce Wayne attending a funeral without the protection of his Batsuit. What made the scene particularly interesting was watching Bruce trying to save somebody's life while surrounded by people who had absolutely no idea what he spent his evenings doing. Of course, there was another moment later in the movie when we were briefly led to believe that Bruce might have to attend a rather more personal funeral, having discovered that the Riddler had sent a package to Wayne Tower that was subsequently opened by Alfred. And it turns out that somebody else in Gotham City is getting a funeral in the sequel.

Sources indicate that as reported by ComicBook, a fresh video from the set of The Batman: Part II has revealed that a funeral scene is being filmed for the upcoming DC sequel, although there's nothing in the footage to indicate whose funeral it actually is. Among the theories being floated by fans are the deaths of Andy Serkis' Alfred Pennyworth and Colin Farrell's Oswald Cobb, while some have even suggested that we could be looking at the funeral of Bruce Wayne himself. There's also every possibility that what we're seeing is a flashback to the funeral of Thomas and Martha Wayne.

It has been revealed that of course, we didn't actually know a great deal about Don Mitchell Jr. when we attended his funeral in the first movie, and the most interesting thing about that scene was what the Riddler had planned for the people attending it. It would also be a little strange to kill off Alfred in the sequel, given that Reeves had already used the prospect of Bruce losing him as a means of getting the two men to open up to one another in the first movie.

In a recent development, four powers, and four completely different kinds of person behind them. Here is what you would wake up with, what it would cost you, and why the MCU keeps handing it to somebody exactly like you.

Recent findings suggest that you get the power that is really about taking the hit so that nobody else has to. Strength in the MCU always lands on people who were already carrying too much, which is exactly why it suits you.

You get the power that never switches off. Spider-sense is a gift and a nervous system on permanent alert, and the people who get it in these films are always the ones who were already worrying about everybody.

Sources indicate that you get the quietest power in the building, and quietly the most useful. Invisibility comes with force fields for a reason, because the people who prefer not to be seen are usually the ones holding a shield around everybody else.

Recent findings suggest that you get the biggest and least comfortable power on the list, the one that runs directly on feeling. Chaos magic is not really a superpower in the MCU so much as an emotional state with consequences attached.

According to recent reports, had this footage emerged six months ago, there probably wouldn't have been quite so many people entertaining the idea that it could be Bruce Wayne's funeral. Since then, though, Pattinson has landed the role of James Bond, we're about to get a latest man in charge of DC Studios, and there's now a different director helping to finish the movie that Reeves started, with Steven Soderbergh having stepped in to help complete production.

By the time we get to see Pattinson in the Batsuit again, it'll have been almost six years since his first outing as the character, and we still don't know whether we'll be getting a third movie. That stated, if you're Warner Bros. and you've made the decision to kill off Batman, would you really film his funeral somewhere that anybody with a phone could record it?

The Batman: Part II is scheduled to arrive in theaters in February 2028. Stay tuned to Collider for more news and updates on the DC Universe.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the Asics Gel-Nimbus 29 swaps in a new midsole foam to deliver a more comfortable and softer ride than its predecessors, and it’s a better easy-run cruiser as a result. However, the new foam is so soft that the Gel-Nimbus 29 is a bit limited compared to bouncier cushioned shoes like the Asics Novablast 6 or Nike Vomero Plus.

In a recent development, why you can trust Tom's Guide Our writers and editors spend hours analyzing and reviewing products, services, and apps to help find what's best for you. Find out more about how we test, analyze, and rate.

The Asics Gel-Nimbus 29 is almost three decades old, and to celebrate, Asics has made the biggest update to the shoe we’ve seen in years.

A new midsole foam is at the heart of the changes, with the FF Luxe Plus material introduced in the Asics Slowcush being rolled down to the Gel-Nimbus 29. It’s a very soft foam and transforms the ride of the Gel-Nimbus 29 compared to past models.

Overall, I rate the newly introduced Nimbus as an upgrade, and the softer ride makes its role clearer in the Asics line-up compared with the more versatile Asics Novablast 6, but the ride did sometimes stray into too-soft territory for my taste.

The Asics Gel-Nimbus 29 released in October 2026 and costs $170 in the U.S. and £170 in the U.K., which is the same price as the Gel-Nimbus 28 in the U.S., while in the U.K. the price has actually gone down by £10.

However, right now you can get the Asics Gel-Nimbus 28 for $129 in Amazon’s sale, and the older shoe is likely to remain around that price now that the fresh model is out.

The Asics Gel-Nimbus 29 is at the moment available in 10 colors for the men’s shoe and 11 for the women’s, and you can pick between wide and standard fits.

I actually tested a full size down from my normal running shoe size by accident, so it did come up a little tight as you’d expect, but I think going with your normal size will be fine.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

The Gel-Nimbus 29 is a max-cushioned shoe and keeps the same stack height as its predecessor, standing 43.5mm tall at the heel and 35.5mm at the forefoot for an 8mm drop.

It’s a little lighter than the previous model, though, and weighs 9.7oz in my US men’s size 9, which is pretty light for such a cushioned shoe.

The Gel-Nimbus 29 has an engineered mesh upper that prioritizes comfort over being lightweight, and it is comfortable thanks to soft, stretchy material and padding around the collar.

I do like that the tongue isn’t overly padded, though, because this makes it feel a bit lighter and less oppressive — the tendency with highly cushioned shoes like this is to also max out the padding on the upper, which I find can make them hot and sweaty at times.

The past four generations of the Gel-Nimbus used FF Blast Plus foam in their midsoles (or the plant-based variant FF Blast Plus Eco), and although the exact makeup and feel of this foam did change between models, they have a similar ride.

You can definitely notice the difference with the introduction of FF Luxe Plus foam in the Gel-Nimbus 29, which still also retains a small slab of PureGel under the heel.

It’s a softer shoe, with a little more bounce than its predecessor as well, and it’s also softer than the Novablast 6 and Gel-Cumulus 28.

Another small update to the Gel-Nimbus 29 is found on its outsole, which has more extensive rubber coverage than past models.

The Hybrid AsicsGrip material has gripped well on slick sidewalks during the British autumn and shows no signs of wear and tear after 35 miles.

I’ve tested every version of the Gel-Nimbus since the 24, and while there have been minor updates in each of the past few years, it’s been a pretty similar experience since FF Blast Plus was introduced with the Gel-Nimbus 25.

That’s not to say it’s been a bad experience, but it's been the same and not all that remarkable when looking around the market, which is full of max-cushioned cruisers.

The Asics Gel-Nimbus 29 does stand out a lot more, both from past models and when compared to other brands’ top-cushioned options, just because it is so soft.

From my first step in the shoe, I could feel myself sinking into the FF Luxe Plus midsole, which is great for delivering a comfortable ride and absorbing the shock of running.

However, it’s not the most responsive foam — the Gel-Nimbus 29 is all about comfort and less about rebound, based on my testing.

On easy runs under an hour long, it felt great, but when I ran at faster paces or did a long run in the Gel-Nimbus 29, the foam started to feel like it was sapping energy rather than bouncing it back.

This is not a versatile shoe like the Novablast 6, which is comfortable but also lively at faster paces. The Gel-Nimbus is a shoe that works very well for easy efforts, but I’d pair it with a faster, firmer shoe for workouts in a running shoe rotation.

If you love a soft running shoe, the Asics Gel-Nimbus 29 is one of the softest I’ve tried, and it’s certainly a comfortable pick for racking up the miles.

It’s actually a little too soft for my preferences; I’d rather use the firmer, more responsive Novablast 6 or bouncier Nike Vomero Plus for daily training, but I’m sure many runners will love the feel of the Gel-Nimbus 29.

Given its high price, I'd also be tempted to look at cheaper cushioned options, though, like the Kiprun Kipride Max or Hoka Clifton Pro, which both have smoother rides and more energetic foams in their midsole.

I’ve not tested the Asics Slowcush myself, but given it uses an even higher stack of the FF Luxe Plus foam found in the Gel-Nimbus 29, I’m sure it would be a good alternative for those chasing the softest ride possible.

The changes to the Gel-Nimbus 29 were long overdue, though, and I think it now stands out more as a premium cushioned option, both within the Asics line-up and when compared to rivals from other brands.

Industry observers note that apple’s iPad lineup is incredibly strong, and two standout options are the iPad Air and iPad Pro. If you’re trying to decide whether the iPad Pro is worth the extra cost this holiday season, here’s everything you need to know.

Bonus pick: The all-upcoming iPad mini is up to $100 off for Black Friday as well.

Apple updated the iPad Air earlier this year, bringing the M4 chip for improved performance along with 12GB of RAM, up from 8GB in the previous generation.

Sources indicate that the iPad Air is available in 11-inch and 13-inch screen sizes, and uses an LCD display with a 60Hz refresh rate. This means it doesn’t offer OLED or ProMotion, unlike the iPad Pro. It uses Touch ID for biometric authentication, supports the Magic Keyboard and Apple Pencil Pro, and offers the full iPadOS multitasking experience.

According to recent reports, the iPad Air is available in four colors: blue, purple, starlight, and space gray. It starts at 128GB of storage and can be configured up to 1TB.

The iPad Pro is the best iPad money can buy. It’s powered by Apple’s M5 chip and offers many advantages over the iPad Air.

The biggest difference is the display technology. The iPad Pro is available in 11-inch and 13-inch sizes and uses Apple’s Ultra Retina XDR display with tandem OLED technology. This means it offers deeper blacks, better contrast, and higher brightness than the LCD screen found in the iPad Air.

The iPad Pro also supports ProMotion with adaptive refresh rates up to 120Hz. This means scrolling, animations, Apple Pencil interactions, and more will be significantly smoother.

It has been revealed that contrary to what the naming implies, the iPad Pro is also noticeably thinner and lighter than the iPad Air. The 11-inch iPad Pro measures 5.3mm thick, while the 13-inch model is even thinner at 5.1mm.

The iPad Pro offers Face ID instead of Touch ID, Thunderbolt connectivity, a four-speaker audio system, and nano-texture display options with the higher-end configuration.

For most people, the iPad Air is the right choice. It delivers the entire iPad experience, excellent performance, and comes in four fun colors and two different screen sizes.

Sources indicate that the iPad Pro is the best iPad you can buy, but it’s overkill for most people. Don’t get me wrong, I love my iPad Pro. If it’s in your holiday budget, it’s a fantastic choice. I can’t overstate how impressive the tandem OLED display is. It’s significantly better than the LCD screen on the iPad Air. It’s also great having Face ID in the iPad form factor.

The iPad Pro is slightly more tempting at its current sale price, with the mid-range 13-inch model at an impressive $350 off.

Sources indicate that still, both the iPad Air and iPad Pro run the same iPadOS experience, and that’s why I think the iPad Air is the better value for most people. What do you think? Let us know down in the comments.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that one of the most iconic anime series of all time is coming to Blu-ray for the very first time. The series gave rise to space opera series like Mobile Suit Gundam and Macross, and now two of its sequel series have been painstakingly restored in HD. Space Battleship Yamamoto II and III are coming to Blu-Ray in Japan next year.

Debuting in 1974, Space Battleship Yamamoto is set in the year 2199; Earth has been devastated by the warlike alien Gamilons, but a message from space offers technology that can restore the planet to health. Unfortunately, humanity will have to travel further into the stars than ever before to reach it. Using the "wave motion engine" plans in the message, the Earth Federation salvages the sunken WWII battleship Yamamoto and rebuilds it into a powerful spacecraft that sets out to save humanity's future. The series was a hit, and concluded with Farewell to Space Battleship Yamamoto, a movie that saw the Yamamoto and her crew sacrifice themselves in a blaze of glory to defeat an alien menace.

It has been revealed that however, the final fate of the Yamamoto's characters was very unpopular, and a second season of the show, dubbed Space Battleship Yamamoto II, was commissioned; it overwrote the movie for further adventures of the ship and her crew as they battled the Comet Empire. It was successful enough that a third season, Space Battleship Yamamoto III, was produced; it saw peace emerge between humanity and the Gamilons as they united to fight a common foe. Now, both series are coming to Blu-ray for the first time in Japan; all 26 episodes of II will be released on March 26, 2027, with the 25 episodes of III following on June 23, 2027. Both will be available in a box set with a collectible booklet, and will retail for 44,000 yen (roughly $277 USD).

Sources indicate that space Battle Yamamoto, plus sequel series II and III, were re-dubbed, re-edited, and brought over to the United States as Star Blazers in 1979. It was unlike any other animated series American audiences had ever seen; at the time, American cartoons were strictly episodic, while Star Blazers was serialized, with long-running plots and subplots. And even though some content was edited out of the series, it still featured more mature storytelling than American audiences were accustomed to. It paved the way for subsequent anime series to be localized, and served as a stepping stone for the current anime boom.

Space Battleship Yamamoto II and III will be available on Blu-ray in Japan on March 26, 2027, and June 23, 2027, respectively. No international release has yet been declared. Stay tuned to Collider for future updates.

In a recent development, upgrading your TV's sound doesn't necessarily mean spending a fortune on a full home theater setup, especially with early Black Friday deals bringing substantial discounts on soundbars and audio systems from Sony, Bose, Samsung, and LG. Sony has some of the biggest price cuts, with savings of up to 32% across select Bravia Theater models, including more than $700 off its premium Theater Trio system.

Samsung's Dolby Atmos soundbars are also discounted by as much as $400, while Bose and LG have more affordable options for anyone looking to improve dialogue clarity, add some bass, or enjoy surround sound without a complicated setup. Whether you're shopping for a compact speaker for a bedroom TV or a more immersive system for movie nights, here are the deals worth considering.

Industry observers note that for anyone building a premium home theater around a large TV, the Sony Bravia Theater Trio is down to $1,498 from $2,199.99, saving you $701.99, or roughly 32%. Unlike a conventional soundbar, the Trio uses three separate front speakers for the left, center, and right channels, helping spread dialogue and effects across a wider soundstage. You can read PCMag’s “excellent” review for more details.

Industry observers note that the Sony Bravia Theater Bar 7 is down to $718 from $869 for anyone who wants a single soundbar under the TV. Its nine speakers include upward- and side-firing drivers that widen the soundstage and give Dolby Atmos some height, but there’s no subwoofer, so the now $898 Bar 7 with a wireless sub bundle (down from $1,099.99) might be the better pick for deeper bass.

Moving down Sony's lineup, the Bravia Theater Bar 6 is $548, down from $699.99, and pairs a 3.1.2-channel soundbar with a wireless subwoofer and upward-firing speakers for Dolby Atmos height effects. Spending $100 more gets you the Bravia Theater System 6, now $648 from $799.99, which adds rear speakers in a 5.1-channel setup for movies and games where sound moves behind you.

Industry observers note that for a more affordable upgrade, the Sony Bravia Theater Bar 5 is down to $278 from $349.99, saving you nearly $72. It's a 3.1-channel system with a dedicated center speaker and wireless subwoofer, so dialogue should come through more clearly while music and movie effects get some additional low-end presence.

In a recent development, sony’s older systems are discounted too, including the HT-S400 at $258, down from $299, which pairs a 2.1-channel soundbar and wireless subwoofer with S-Force Pro Front Surround to widen the sound for everyday TV, sports, and casual movies. The HT-S40R is arguably the better deal at the same $258, down from $329.99, since it adds two rear speakers for a full 5.1-channel setup, though neither model supports Dolby Atmos.

In a recent development, for smaller rooms or for anyone who mainly wants dialogue to come across more clearly, Bose has two compact soundbars on sale: The newer Bose TV Speaker (2nd Gen) is down to $239 from $299, with an updated acoustic design that Bose indicates improves clarity and overall sound performance. Meanwhile, the original Bose TV Speaker is $199, down from $279, and offers a similarly compact design with a dedicated dialogue mode and adjustable bass.

Samsung’s HW-Q800H is down to $697.99 from $1,097.99, a $400 cut on a 5.1.2-channel Dolby Atmos soundbar with a wireless subwoofer. Its side- and upward-firing speakers help place effects around and above you, while a dedicated center channel keeps dialogue clear during busy action scenes.

In a recent development, for something that takes up less space, the Samsung HW-S60D is $277.99, down from $399.99, and fits seven speakers, including side-firing drivers, into a compact 5.0-channel soundbar. It also supports Dolby Atmos, Adaptive Sound, and a voice enhancement mode, along with Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, AirPlay, and Chromecast for music streaming. That said, it has no upward-firing speakers or subwoofer, so its height effects and bass won’t match that of the Q800H.

If you're looking for a complete surround sound system without spending several hundred dollars, the LG S6FTR is down to $249.99 from $399.99, saving you $150, or roughly 38%. It's a 5.1-channel home theater package with a soundbar, subwoofer, and dedicated rear speakers. That makes it particularly appealing for action movies and games, where directional sound adds to the experience.

The LG S40TR is another affordable option for anyone who wants rear speakers included in the box. It's currently $199.99, down from $279.99, and offers a 4.1-channel arrangement with a wireless subwoofer and two rear speakers. This should give movie soundtracks a greater sense of direction than a basic soundbar, while the subwoofer handles the lower frequencies that smaller TV speakers often struggle to reproduce.

At just under $187, the S60T is the least expensive system in this roundup, pairing a 3.1-channel soundbar with a wireless subwoofer for clearer dialogue and fuller sound than your TV’s speakers. That noted, it lacks rear speakers and Dolby Atmos height channels, so it’s better suited to someone who wants a simple, affordable upgrade without filling the room with additional hardware.

Recent findings suggest that in short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Follow our Black Friday coverage for the latest and best deals our team finds. Another good tip is to only buy what you need. It sounds simple, but making a list of the things you want before jumping into a sale with millions of products helps you focus and make smarter decisions.

Black Friday used to be bigger for major retailers and more expensive tech and appliances, while Cyber Monday was better for cheaper tech and gave smaller businesses a chance to compete online. Nowadays, though, the distinction is almost meaningless. Every major retailer will offer sales on both days, and the smart move is to know what you want, do your research, or refer to guides like our Black Friday and Cyber Monday coverage that have done all the vetting for you.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cultured Code is bringing swipe gestures to Things on Apple’s touchscreen MacBook Pro. Version 3.25 builds on the task manager’s basic touch support so you can schedule a to-do with a swipe or select several tasks with two fingers and drag them all at once.

In a recent development, say you’re going through your Today list and want to put something off until tomorrow. Swipe right on the to-do to open the date picker. Open it by touch and you’ll see taller rows that make dates easier to tap. Custom menus get the same treatment.

Swiping left selects a to-do. Swipe left again to deselect it. For a longer list, swipe up or down with two fingers to select several items at once. Then touch and hold any selected item to pick up the whole group, even if some of those tasks are offscreen. You can also drag individual to-dos and headings.

Sources indicate that A single tap selects a to-do, and a second tap expands it. Double-tapping works too. Inside a to-do, checklist items are easier to reorder by touch. You can also cancel a to-do or checklist item by pressing and holding its checkbox.

Cultured Code has also made the sidebar easier to resize with a finger and given buttons throughout the Mac app larger tap targets.

The update follows Siri AI and Spotlight integration in Things 3.24 and more flexible scheduling for repeating to-dos in Things 3.23. You can find Things for Mac on the Mac App Store.

They're $149 on Walmart as an Black Friday deal, down from $249 and matching their lowest price ever.

This TV supports Dolby Vision and Dolby Atmos, and if you're a gamer, you get a refresh rate of 240Hz that is automatically triggered with its Auto Game Mode feature.

It's a solid choice for gaming, especially at this price point.

Industry observers note that alienware makes great gaming laptops, and the Aurora is a great option for anyone who wants to get all the essentials without spending too much. At its current $1,099 price (originally $1,999), the Alienware Aurora 16 becomes a mid-tier gaming laptop at a "budget" price. We reviewed the higher-tier Aurora 16X and were impressed with it. The Aurora 16 has a slightly slower processor, a dimmer display with half the refresh rate, a smaller battery, and a weaker graphics card, but given its price, it's great for a gamer looking for a solid gaming laptop in the $1,000 range.

Amazon has a much larger inventory of tech products on sale, but the ones they both sell are mostly priced the same. While Amazon may have more deals, Walmart usually has a couple of surprise flagship tech products on sale that Amazon will later price match. So taking all of that into consideration, the best one will be whichever has whatever you're looking to buy at the lower price.

Last year, Apple officially confirmed CarPlay Ultra, the next-generation version of CarPlay that it first teased way back at WWDC 2022.

CarPlay Ultra first launched for Aston Martin owners in the United States and Canada. What about other automakers? Here’s what we know.

9to5Mac is supported by Sony: Score Sony’s ULT Field 1 Bluetooth speaker for 51% off. Powerful bass, room-filling sound, up to 12 hours of battery life, IP67 durability, stereo pairing support, and much more.

Updated November 24, 2026: Latest on Hyundai, more.

Industry observers note that in December 2023, Apple noted that Porsche and Aston Martin would be the first automakers to support next-generation CarPlay starting in 2024. That deadline came and went, and Apple confirmed in January that next-gen CarPlay had been delayed but was still in development.

Apple doesn’t offer a timeline on when CarPlay Ultra will actually be available through any other brand beyond Aston Martin. The organization also does not have a dedicated list of automakers that have signed on to support CarPlay Ultra listed on its website.

When Apple confirmed the next-generation version of CarPlay at WWDC 2022, however, it stated that several brands had committed to supporting the platform. In May of last year, Apple touted that three new partners had signed on: Hyundai, Kia, and Genesis.

In a recent development, however, several brands have also dropped their plans to support CarPlay Ultra. Mercedes-Benz was originally on Apple’s list, but abandoned its plans to support next-generation CarPlay in 2024. According to the Financial Times, Audi, Volvo, Polestar, and Renault have also decided against supporting CarPlay Ultra, despite originally being touted as partners by Apple.

With all of that stated, here is the full list of automakers who proposal to eventually support CarPlay Ultra, as of November 2026.

What do we know beyond this list? Not a whole lot. Interestingly, Top Gear reported that the Hyundai IONIQ 3 EV would support CarPlay Ultra. Hyundai revealed the IONIQ 3 in April, but has not commented on whether the vehicle will support CarPlay Ultra as rumors suggested.

Mark Gurman at Bloomberg has also reported CarPlay Ultra will launch for “least one major latest Hyundai/Kia model in the second half of this year.”.

While Apple has touted Ford as a partner for CarPlay Ultra, the automaker recently signaled it’s not too impressed with the first version of a platform.

In a recent interview, Ford CEO Jim Farley was asked whether the firm is “considering” CarPlay Ultra support. Here’s what he said:.

“We are. We don’t like the execution in round 1 of Ultra, but we’re very committed to Apple. I’ve talked to Tim many times about this.”.

It’s better than a flat “no,” but perhaps not the enthusiasm Ford drivers might have hoped to hear.

The question at this point is whether any other automakers have ditched CarPlay Ultra. Ideally, Apple will provide a full list sooner rather than later, but in the meantime, this is the only information we have.

If you're thinking of picking up any substantial-ticket items—whether for yourself or as a gift for someone on your list—I would advise you not to sleep on Walmart's sale. Walmart was the first major retailer to announce and kick off its Black Friday and Cyber Monday sale for 2026, and they're holding three major shopping events through the December holidays.

Walmart will hold three sales between Nov. 12 and Dec. 2, as outlined in a recent press release. The sales will be both online and in-store, and will target a mix of Walmart+ members and general shoppers.

The events will take place on three different dates:.

Walmart's Black Friday Deals Event 1: Nov. 12–15.

Available online and in stores starting at 6 a.m. local time.

Walmart+ members get six hours of early access beginning online at 12:01 a.m. ET on Nov. 12.

According to recent reports, walmart's Black Friday Deals Event 2: Nov. 23–29.

Sources indicate that online only: Nov. 23 starting at 12:01 a.m. ET.

Online and in stores: Nov. 27 starting at 6 a.m. local time.

Walmart+ members get six hours of early access online beginning Nov. 23 at 12:01 a.m. ET.

Sources indicate that walmart's Cyber Monday Deals Event: Nov. 30-Dec. 2.

In a recent development, walmart's physical stores will open at 6:00 a.m. local time on Nov. 27 for their Black Friday events. Of course, they will start online earlier, so make sure to check their website as well.

It has been revealed that walmart says that they will have discounts on electronics, toys, fashion, beauty, home goods, gifts, and everyday essentials. Although the company doesn't provide much in the way of specifics in its press release, last year's sales included discounts on TCL TVs, Dyson vacuums, Dreo appliances, and toys from LEGO.

Walmart's first sale already features plenty of good deals; you don't need to wait for Nov. 27 to start to find some products going for their lowest prices ever. Here are some of the best ones I've found so far:.

Recent findings suggest that deals are both online and in the physical stores. There might be deals online that you won't see in-store and vice versa.

According to recent reports, the holiday season will see major sales from the same list of retailers that compete for your dollars throughout the year—namely, Best Buy, Target, and Amazon. Each will have its own version of Black Friday and Cyber Monday sales. So far, only Walmart has revealed its plans.

According to recent reports, in short, yes. Though they aren't quite as impactful as they once were, Black Friday and Cyber Monday sales offer discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. Whether it's a major purchase you've been saving up for or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts, especially on items like appliances and electronics. Last year's sales included categories such as tech, home improvement, and fitness.

It has been revealed that black Friday used to be when major retailers offered their best deals on expensive tech and appliances, while Cyber Monday was for cheaper tech and gave smaller businesses a chance to compete online. Now, however, the distinction is almost meaningless: Every major retailer offers sales on both days, which means the smart move is to know what you want, use price trackers to monitor the deals, and refer to our Black Friday coverage, where we do all the searching, curating, and price tracking for you.
